items.headline: Global copper price averaged $14,473 a ton in September, a series high
items.take: FRED's monthly global copper price averaged $14,473.06 per metric ton in September, up 1.0% from $14,331.26 in August and 44.8% from September 2025. It is the highest reading in the series, which begins in January 2000. A three-month climb from $13,542.82 in July is the kind of input-cost pressure manufacturers and electrical-equipment makers track.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (global price of copper)

items.headline: Global wheat price rose to $246.85 a ton in September, up 3.8% on the month
items.take: FRED's monthly global wheat price averaged $246.85 per metric ton in September, up 3.8% from $237.86 in August and 59.1% above September 2025. It is the highest monthly reading since July 2023 and the fourth straight rise from $199.65 in June. Grain costs feed into food prices with a lag, a point worth watching alongside the maize series, which also rose in September.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (global price of wheat)

items.headline: Fed funds rate 3.88% sits 138 bp above the ECB deposit rate of 2.50%
items.take: The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on Nov. 24, while the ECB deposit facility rate stood at 2.50% on the same date, a gap of 1.38 percentage points. The ECB rate was raised from 2.25% to 2.50% in September and has been unchanged since, per FRED. The two central banks are at different points in their cycles, which keeps policy-rate differentials in view for currency and bond markets.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DFF and ECBDFR)

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield 103 bp above the fed funds rate on Nov. 24, from 122 bp a week earlier
items.take: The 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield was 4.91% on Nov. 24 against an effective federal funds rate of 3.88%, a 1.03 percentage-point gap. On Nov. 17 the yield was 5.10% with the funds rate also at 3.88%, a gap of 1.22 points. The narrowing came entirely from the long end, since the policy rate did not move.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS10 and DFF)

items.headline: ECB account: euro area HICP 3.8% in September, energy 18.9%, core 2.5%
items.take: The ECB's account of its 28-29 October meeting, published Nov. 26, says headline HICP inflation rose to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August, with energy inflation at 18.9% from 14.3%. Core inflation edged up to 2.5% from 2.4%, and services inflation rose to 3.2%. The account says there were no material signs of second-round effects so far. AlphaGen read: the Governing Council still saw the energy shock as mostly direct, but flagged that indirect effects should become more material over time.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: ECB account: markets priced a deposit-rate peak near 3% vs one more hike in survey
items.take: The account of the ECB's October meeting says that after the September meeting the OIS curve briefly priced in more than four additional 25 bp hikes over 12 months, then pared back to just under three. Term-premia-adjusted market pricing pointed to a deposit facility rate peak around 3%, while the Survey of Monetary Analysts median foresaw only one more hike. AlphaGen read: market pricing and the analyst survey differed by roughly two hikes at the time of the meeting.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: ECB account: Brent up 13% to $115 since September, gas 22% higher at €97/MWh
items.take: The ECB account of its 28-29 October meeting says front-month Brent futures had risen 13% to USD 115 per barrel since the September meeting, and gas prices had risen 22% to €97 per MWh. The euro had depreciated 4.0% against the US dollar over the same period, and 2.2% in nominal effective terms. AlphaGen read: these are the ECB's figures as of late October, not current market levels.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: ECB account: bank use of standard refinancing at highest level since end-2016
items.take: The ECB's account says that on Oct. 27, 2026, recourse to the Eurosystem's standard refinancing operations had risen to its highest level since the end of 2016, with short-term money market rates close to the deposit facility rate. The account calls this a comforting sign that banks are becoming more accustomed to using standard operations as excess liquidity falls. AlphaGen read: as excess liquidity declines, banks are drawing more on regular ECB operations.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: BoE FPC: hyperscaler bond issuance set to top $305B in 2026, about 8% of global IG
items.take: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee record, published Nov. 26 for its Nov. 19 meeting, says hyperscaler bond issuance is set to exceed $305 billion in 2026, around 8% of global investment grade issuance. The FPC says AI-related financing is increasingly complex, circular and opaque, making it more likely that stress in one area propagates to another. AlphaGen read: the FPC is treating the financing structure of the AI buildout, not only its pace, as a stability question.
items.source_name: Bank of England

items.headline: BoE FPC: gilt yields rise reflects expected policy rates, not term premia
items.take: The FPC record says government bond yields have reached near two-decade highs in several advanced economies. In the UK, it says the rise has mainly reflected higher expected policy rates, driven by higher energy prices and resilient growth, rather than higher term premia, while fiscal and political uncertainty weighed more in France. AlphaGen read: the FPC says gilt and gilt repo markets have functioned well, with hedge fund leverage still elevated by historical standards.
items.source_name: Bank of England

items.headline: BLS schedules November CPI for Dec. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS says the Consumer Price Index news release for November 2026 is scheduled to be published on Thursday, Dec. 10, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. In October the CPI-U rose 0.4% seasonally adjusted after 0.6% in September, and the index excluding food and energy rose 0.3% for a third straight month. AlphaGen read: the November report will show whether the 0.3% core pace held.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics

items.headline: BLS schedules November jobs report for Dec. 4 at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS says the Employment Situation for November 2026 is scheduled to be published on Friday, Dec. 4, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The October report showed total nonfarm payroll employment up 165,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.1%. AlphaGen read: the November figures are the next hard labor-market read after October's 165,000 gain.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics

items.headline: Fed funds rate 3.88% sits about 0.6 point above core PCE inflation of 3.3%
items.take: FRED shows the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% on Nov. 24, and BEA reported that the October PCE price index excluding food and energy rose 3.3% from a year earlier. The difference is about 0.58 percentage point (computed from the rounded inflation figure). AlphaGen read: by this simple measure the policy rate is only modestly above core inflation, which frames how the Fed may weigh its next decision.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis; Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Implied 5-year, 5-years-forward inflation rate about 2.11% on Nov. 25, from 2.15% a week earlier
items.take: FRED's 10-year breakeven inflation rate was 2.12% on Nov. 25 and the 5-year was 2.13%; on Nov. 18 they were 2.19% and 2.23%. Doubling the 10-year rate and subtracting the 5-year gives an approximate 5-year, 5-years-forward rate of 2.11%, against 2.15% on Nov. 18 (computed, rounded inputs). AlphaGen read: longer-horizon inflation compensation eased by about 4 bp over the week, and by less than the 10 bp drop in the 5-year rate.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 2-year and 30-year Treasury yields both fell about 16-17 bp in a week; 2s30s gap 67 bp
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.63% on Nov. 24, down from 4.80% on Nov. 17, while the 30-year was 5.30%, down from 5.46%. That is a 17 bp fall at the short end and 16 bp at the long end, leaving the 30-year minus 2-year gap at 67 bp versus 66 bp (computed from the rounded yields). AlphaGen read: the decline was close to a parallel shift, not a steepening or flattening of the curve.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: New-home supply 8.0 months in October, from 9.3 in September, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's Census series for monthly supply of new houses reads 8.0 months for October, against 9.3 for September and 8.5 for August. The September figure is now 9.3, versus the 8.4 AlphaGen reported from the same series on Nov. 24. AlphaGen read: the one-month drop of 1.3 months (computed) is large, but the September base has changed, so the series is worth rechecking against Census's own tables.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), Census Bureau data

items.headline: GDPNow Q4 2026 reading is 2.90% on FRED, down from 3.21% on Nov. 20
items.take: FRED's GDPNow series now shows 2.9019% for the fourth quarter of 2026, compared with 3.2093% in AlphaGen's Nov. 20 item from the same series, a drop of 0.31 percentage point (computed). The third-quarter reading in the series is 3.2721%. AlphaGen read: GDPNow is the Atlanta Fed's model-based estimate and moves with each data release, so it is a tracking tool, not an official GDP figure.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), Atlanta Fed GDPNow

items.headline: Dollar value of one pound 1.3104 on Nov. 20, down from 1.3322 on Nov. 10
items.take: FRED's daily series shows U.S. dollars per British pound at 1.3104 on Nov. 20, its lowest in the readings from Nov. 10 and below 1.3217 on Nov. 17 and 1.3322 on Nov. 10. Over the same span, dollars per euro went from 1.1153 to 1.0981. AlphaGen read: the pound and the euro both fell against the dollar over those ten days, consistent with the stronger broad dollar index AlphaGen has been tracking.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), Board of Governors H.10

items.headline: Chicago Fed financial conditions index -0.444 for week of Nov. 20, up for a seventh week
items.take: FRED's National Financial Conditions Index reads -0.444 for the week of Nov. 20, from -0.450 on Nov. 13 and -0.492 on Oct. 2. It has risen in each of the last seven weekly readings, a 0.048 point increase since Oct. 2 (computed). AlphaGen read: negative readings mean conditions looser than the long-run average, so the index is still on the loose side but drifting toward average.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), Chicago Fed NFCI

items.headline: WTI fell $6.17 to $81.42 on Nov. 23 as Brent-WTI gap hit $9.78
items.take: FRED shows WTI at $81.42 per barrel on Nov. 23, down $6.17 from $87.59 on Nov. 20, while Brent eased $1.56 to $91.20. The Brent-WTI gap widened to $9.78, the widest of the six readings from Nov. 17 ($3.41) through Nov. 24 ($9.56). AlphaGen read: the move came almost entirely in the U.S. benchmark, so the gap says more about WTI than about a broad shift in global crude.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Brent at $91.80 on Nov. 24, $3.37 below its Nov. 19 reading of $95.17
items.take: FRED shows Brent at $95.17 per barrel on Nov. 19, up $2.29 from $92.88 on Nov. 18 and the highest of the readings from Nov. 17 to Nov. 24. It was $91.80 on Nov. 24, a $3.37 decline, after $91.20 on Nov. 23. AlphaGen read: a spot series that moves a few dollars in either direction in a week is a reminder that fuel-cost swings can reverse quickly.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate 7.21%, 11 bp below Oct. 22 but 10 bp above the Nov. 12 low
items.take: FRED's 30-year mortgage rate series reads 7.21% for Nov. 25, versus 7.32% on Oct. 22 and 7.11% on Nov. 12, the lowest of the six readings since Oct. 22. The rate is 11 basis points lower than on Oct. 22 and 10 basis points higher than on Nov. 12. AlphaGen read: borrowing costs have eased over five weeks but have not kept falling since the mid-November low.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 2-year Treasury yield 69 bp above SOFR on Nov. 24, from 88 bp on Nov. 17
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.63% and SOFR at 3.94% on Nov. 24, a 69 basis point gap. On Nov. 17 the readings were 4.80% and 3.92%, an 88 basis point gap. AlphaGen read: the gap narrowed by 19 basis points because the 2-year yield fell while the overnight rate stayed within 2 basis points, so markets are pricing less distance between overnight and two-year borrowing.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 10-year yield fell 12 bp on Nov. 20; real yield accounted for 11 bp, breakeven 1 bp
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.92% on Nov. 20, down 12 basis points from 5.04% on Nov. 19. The 10-year real yield fell 11 basis points to 2.77% from 2.88%, and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate eased 1 basis point to 2.15% from 2.16%. AlphaGen read: nearly all of the one-day drop reflected the real component rather than inflation expectations.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: High-yield spread 274 bp over investment grade on Nov. 24, from 251 bp on Nov. 17
items.take: FRED shows the high-yield option-adjusted spread at 3.72 points on Nov. 24 and the investment-grade spread at 0.98, a 2.74-point gap. On Nov. 17 the readings were 3.43 and 0.92, a 2.51-point gap, so the difference widened 23 basis points. AlphaGen read: the gap, which isolates extra compensation for junk-rated risk, widened even as Treasury yields fell over the same stretch.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Initial jobless claims 4-week average 196,000 for week ended Nov. 21, from 197,500
items.take: FRED's weekly initial claims readings were 195,000 (Oct. 24), 191,000 (Oct. 31), 202,000 (Nov. 7), 202,000 (Nov. 14) and 189,000 (Nov. 21). AlphaGen's calculation puts the four-week average at 196,000 for the week ended Nov. 21, versus 197,500 for the four weeks ended Nov. 14. AlphaGen read: smoothing the weekly swings, claims show little change over the past month.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 30-year minus 10-year Treasury yield gap 39 bp on Nov. 24, from 36 bp on Nov. 17
items.take: FRED shows the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.30% and the 10-year at 4.91% on Nov. 24, a 39-basis-point gap. On Nov. 17 the yields were 5.46% and 5.10%, a 36-basis-point gap. AlphaGen read: the long end fell slightly less than the 10-year over the week, widening the gap by 3 basis points.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: EIA: global refinery inputs fell 4.8M b/d in 2Q26, then rose 1.8M b/d in 3Q26
items.take: EIA, citing Kpler data, says global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (6%) in the second quarter of 2026 after the start of conflict in the Middle East in late February. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows. AlphaGen read: the third-quarter rebound recovered part, not all, of the second-quarter drop.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 3, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: over 16% of new 2026 utility-scale solar is co-located with batteries, vs 2% in 2017
items.take: EIA reports that as of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar photovoltaic capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017. The data come from EIA-860M operator reports. AlphaGen read: developers are increasingly pairing storage with new solar builds.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Oct. 30, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury yields Nov. 24: 2-year 4.63%, 10-year 4.91%, 30-year 5.30%
items.take: FRED's Nov. 24 readings show the 2-year at 4.63%, the 10-year at 4.91% and the 30-year at 5.30%. Against Nov. 17 (4.80%, 5.10%, 5.46%), that is declines of 17, 19 and 16 basis points. AlphaGen read: the move was close to parallel, so the 10-year-minus-2-year gap barely changed.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 10-year yield down 16 bp since Nov. 18: real yield -9 bp, breakeven -7 bp
items.take: The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.91% on Nov. 24, down from 5.07% on Nov. 18, FRED shows. The 10-year inflation-indexed (real) yield slipped to 2.79% from 2.88% and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate to 2.12% from 2.19% over the same dates. AlphaGen read: roughly 9 of the 16 basis points came from real yields and 7 from lower inflation compensation.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Brent-WTI gap $9.56 on Nov. 24 vs $3.41 on Nov. 17 as WTI fell $7.29
items.take: FRED shows WTI at $82.24 per barrel on Nov. 24 versus $89.53 on Nov. 17, a $7.29 decline, while Brent was $91.80 versus $92.94, down $1.14. The gap between the two benchmarks therefore widened to $9.56 from $3.41. AlphaGen read: the weekly drop was concentrated in the U.S. benchmark rather than in Brent.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Henry Hub natural gas $3.30 per MMBtu on Nov. 24, up from $3.10 on Nov. 17
items.take: FRED's Henry Hub spot series reads $3.30 per million Btu on Nov. 24, versus $3.10 on Nov. 17, a gain of $0.20. The window high was $3.31 on Nov. 19, and readings since Nov. 20 have held between $3.28 and $3.30. AlphaGen read: spot gas has steadied in a narrow band over the past four sessions.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: BEA: Q3 real GDP 4.3% annualized is 1.1% quarterly; third estimate due Dec. 23
items.take: BEA's second estimate puts third-quarter real GDP growth at 4.3% at an annual rate, which it states is 1.1% at a quarterly rate, after 2.2% in the second quarter. The release attributes the investment revision to an upward revision to intellectual property products, notably software, based primarily on revisions to BLS's Producer Price Index for system and application software publishing. The next release, the third estimate with industries and corporate profits, is scheduled for Dec. 23, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. EST. AlphaGen read: the 1.1% quarterly figure is the one to compare with unannualized monthly and quarterly series.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis

items.headline: 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread 0.24 pt on Nov. 25, from 0.28 a day earlier
items.take: FRED's 10-year minus 2-year Treasury constant maturity spread (T10Y2Y) was 0.24 percentage point on Nov. 25, down 4 basis points from 0.28 on Nov. 24 and 5 basis points below 0.29 on Nov. 23. It is the lowest of the six daily readings from Nov. 18 to Nov. 25. AlphaGen read: the gap between the two yields narrowed to its smallest in that window.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: 10-year breakeven inflation rate 2.12% on Nov. 25, flat on the day, from 2.19% on Nov. 18
items.take: FRED's 10-year breakeven inflation rate (T10YIE) was 2.12% on Nov. 25, unchanged from Nov. 24 and 1 basis point below 2.13% on Nov. 23. Against 2.19% on Nov. 18 it is 7 basis points lower across the six readings from Nov. 18 to Nov. 25. AlphaGen read: the measure fell on each reading but one in the window and held steady on the latest day.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Census flags sample redesign for New Residential Sales starting with January 2027 data
items.take: In a notice dated Nov. 25, 2026, the Census Bureau said the Survey of Construction will complete a scheduled sample redesign with the January 2027 New Residential Sales release on Feb. 24, 2027. Beginning in January 2027, estimates will include housing units selected from the redesigned sample, and Census points to an FAQ for details. AlphaGen read: readers comparing new home sales across that changeover should check Census's FAQ first.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, New Residential Sales

items.headline: Overnight reverse repo take-up $0.300B on Nov. 25, from $0.301B a day earlier
items.take: FRED shows overnight reverse repurchase agreement take-up (RRPONTSYD) at $0.300 billion on Nov. 25, versus $0.301 billion on Nov. 24 and $0.405 billion on Nov. 19. It is the lowest of the six daily readings from Nov. 18 to Nov. 25. AlphaGen read: take-up remains a sub-$1 billion footnote to funding markets.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Mondelez raises CFO Banati's make-whole award cap to $7.35M from $7.0M
items.take: Mondelez disclosed in a Nov. 25 Form 8-K that its compensation committee chair approved on Nov. 20 an increase in the maximum make-whole cash award for CFO Amit Banati from $7,000,000 to $7,350,000, tied to his former employer's claims for repayment of previously paid compensation. The amount includes taxes withheld by that employer that he cannot recover, and the award remains subject to repayment on specified termination events before the second anniversary of his July 1, 2026 start date. AlphaGen read: the change adds $350,000 to the cap.
items.source_name: Mondelez International, Inc., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: American Express director Angelakis to resign from board Dec. 2
items.take: In a Form 8-K filed Nov. 25, American Express said Michael J. Angelakis notified the company that day of his decision to resign from its Board of Directors, effective Dec. 2, 2026, to devote more time to other business activities. The filing gives no other details. AlphaGen read: a routine board-composition disclosure under Item 5.02.
items.source_name: American Express Company, Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: High-yield spread 3.72 pts on Nov. 24 vs 3.63 a day earlier; IG 0.98
items.take: FRED's ICE BofA US High Yield index option-adjusted spread was 3.72 percentage points on Nov. 24, up 9 basis points from 3.63 on Nov. 23 and below the 3.76 reading on Nov. 20. The investment-grade OAS was 0.98, up 1 basis point. AlphaGen read: the gap between the two was 2.74 points, so the high-yield move was not matched in investment grade.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (ICE Data Indices)

items.headline: WTI $82.24, Brent $91.80 per barrel on Nov. 24; WTI up $0.82 on day
items.take: FRED's EIA-sourced daily series show WTI at $82.24 per barrel on Nov. 24, up $0.82 from $81.42 on Nov. 23, and Brent at $91.80 versus $91.20. The Brent-WTI gap was $9.56. AlphaGen read: WTI is $7.29 below its Nov. 17 level of $89.53 even after the small Nov. 24 rebound.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (U.S. Energy Information Administration)

items.headline: Initial jobless claims 189,000 in week ended Nov. 21, down 13,000
items.take: FRED shows seasonally adjusted initial claims at 189,000 for the week ending Nov. 21, versus 202,000 in each of the two prior weeks (Nov. 7 and Nov. 14). The Oct. 31 reading was 191,000. AlphaGen read: filings fell back to the low end of the range seen over the past six weeks, which ran from 189,000 to 202,000.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (U.S. Department of Labor)

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate 7.21% in Nov. 25 reading, down 7 bp from 7.28%
items.take: FRED's Freddie Mac 30-year fixed mortgage rate series shows 7.21% for Nov. 25, versus 7.28% on Nov. 19 and 7.11% on Nov. 12. The 7 basis point decline reverses part of the prior week's 17 basis point rise. AlphaGen read: borrowing costs remain above 7%, a level that keeps pressure on housing affordability.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Freddie Mac PMMS)

items.headline: ECB study: cards 45% of euro area shop payments in 2026, cash 44%
items.take: The ECB's SPACE study, published Nov. 25, found physical cards accounted for 45% of payments in shops versus 44% for cash, the first time since comparable data began in 2016 that cards led. Mobile payments rose to 9% from 6% in 2024, and 62% of respondents value the option of paying with cash. AlphaGen read: usage is shifting to digital while stated preferences stay split, which is the backdrop for the ECB's work on cash and a possible digital euro.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: NXP completes €1.0B notes offering: 4.625% due 2034, 4.875% due 2037
items.take: NXP and its issuer subsidiaries completed an underwritten public offering on Nov. 24 of €500 million of 4.625% Senior Notes due 2034 and €500 million of 4.875% Senior Notes due 2037. The company intends to use net proceeds for general corporate purposes, which may include capital expenditures or debt repurchases or repayments. AlphaGen read: the 2037 tranche carries a coupon 25 basis points above the 2034 tranche.
items.source_name: NXP Semiconductors N.V., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: American Tower completes €1.2B notes: 4.200% due 2031, 4.500% due 2034
items.take: American Tower completed a registered offering of €600.0 million of 4.200% senior unsecured notes due 2031 and €600.0 million of 4.500% notes due 2034, with aggregate net proceeds of approximately €1,191.3 million after commissions and estimated expenses. The company intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including refinancing upcoming euro maturities. AlphaGen read: the use of proceeds points to euro-maturity refinancing as the stated driver.
items.source_name: American Tower Corp., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: ECB and Riksbank sign agreement for Sweden to join T2; migration targeted Feb 2030
items.take: The ECB and Sveriges Riksbank concluded a T2 currency participation agreement, signed by ECB President Christine Lagarde and Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen, that will let large-value payments in Swedish kronor settle in T2. Migration is targeted for February 2030, and T2 already supports large-value payments in Danish kroner. AlphaGen read: Sweden would move large-value settlement from a national platform to shared European infrastructure, with payments still settled in kronor in central bank money.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Agencies lift 2027 higher-priced mortgage appraisal exemption threshold to $35,500
items.take: The CFPB, Federal Reserve Board and OCC announced that the 2027 threshold for higher-priced mortgage loans subject to special appraisal requirements will increase from $34,200 to $35,500, effective January 1, 2027. The adjustment is based on the same 3.9 percent CPI-W increase as of June 1, 2026. AlphaGen read: loans at or below the threshold are exempt from the special appraisal requirements, so the higher figure widens that exemption slightly.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board / CFPB / OCC

items.headline: Fed, CFPB set 2027 Reg Z and Reg M threshold at $76,300 on 3.9% CPI-W rise
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board and the CFPB announced that Regulation Z (Truth in Lending) and Regulation M (Consumer Leasing) will generally apply to consumer credit transactions and consumer leases of $76,300 or less in 2027, based on a 3.9 percent annual increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026. Private education loans and loans secured by real property remain subject to Regulation Z regardless of amount. AlphaGen read: the threshold is indexed annually to CPI-W, so it moves with that inflation measure.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board / CFPB

items.headline: Analog Devices FY26 revenue $15.18B, up 38%; operating margin 38.6% vs 26.6%
items.take: Analog Devices reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $15,179 million versus $11,020 million in fiscal 2025, operating income of $5,858 million versus $2,932 million, and diluted EPS of $10.21 versus $4.56. Its reported operating margin was 38.6% versus 26.6%. AlphaGen read: operating income roughly doubled on a 38% revenue gain, so the full-year story is margin expansion as much as sales.
items.source_name: Analog Devices (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Analog Devices returned $5.41B in FY26 against $5.45B of free cash flow
items.take: Analog Devices reported fiscal 2026 operating cash flow of $6,186 million and free cash flow of $5,453 million, 41% and 36% of revenue. It returned $5,413 million to shareholders, made up of $2,088 million in dividends and $3,324 million in stock repurchases. AlphaGen read: cash returned equaled about 99% of free cash flow for the year.
items.source_name: Analog Devices (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Bowman: AI can speed supervision, but more information is not better supervision
items.take: In a pre-recorded address to the ASBA-BCBS-FSI meeting in Brasilia, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said artificial intelligence and advanced analytics have the potential to improve the identification of emerging risks, and can give supervisors more information more quickly. items.take: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the independent SVB review found a mismatch between decisionmaking authority and accountability in a structure spanning the Board, the 12 Reserve Banks and numerous committees. items.headline: Bowman: Fed's supervisory principles refocus on material risks, not process volume

items.headline: CFTC staff advisory: bitcoin, ether, stablecoins may count toward 12-month resources
items.take: CFTC staff said on Nov. 23 that certain crypto assets, including bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins, may be counted, subject to appropriate haircuts, toward the requirement that swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations hold financial resources covering at least 12 months of operating costs. The advisory says crypto assets do not count as "cash" or "highly liquid securities" under GAAP and so are not eligible toward the separate liquidity requirement. It represents staff views only and creates no new rules (Staff Letter No. 26-31). AlphaGen read: the guidance addresses how exchanges and clearinghouses may hold reserves, not how customers trade.

items.headline: CFTC approves final rule on data reporting for certain event contracts
items.take: The CFTC announced approval on Nov. 23 of a final rule amending Parts 15, 16 and 17 that sets an alternate reporting framework for certain fully collateralized event contracts, which have been covered by staff no-action letters since 2017. It adds a new Section 16.03, "Covered Event Contracts"; compliance dates run from 60 days after Federal Register publication, with some provisions the later of that date or July 26, 2027, and Section 16.03(g) at 12 months. AlphaGen read: the rule moves reporting for these contracts from no-action relief into the Commission's regulations.
