AlphaGen read: the front end of the curve is pricing a policy path well above today's range, consistent with the FOMC minutes' emphasis on elevated inflation.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury yields and Federal Reserve target range via FRED (DGS2, DFEDTARU, DFF)

items.headline: 10-year minus 3-month Treasury gap is 70 bp on Nov. 19, down from 83 bp on Nov. 13
items.take: FRED data show the 10-year yield at 5.04% and the 3-month bill at 4.34% on Nov. 19, a 70 bp gap, versus 5.15% and 4.32% (83 bp) on Nov. 13 and 4.86% and 4.19% (67 bp) on Nov. 6. The narrowing came from the 10-year easing 11 bp while the 3-month rose 2 bp. AlphaGen read: the long end gave back part of its early-November rise while bills stayed anchored near 4.3%.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury yields via FRED (DGS10, DGS3MO)

items.headline: Fed note: AI-driven productivity optimism does not explain the rise in 10-year yields
items.take: A Nov. 20 FEDS Note by Antoine Lepetit and David Miller finds the 10-year Treasury yield falls after a positive productivity news shock, and that the real 10-year yield actually rose only 90 basis points between 2022Q3 and 2026Q2, against a model-implied forecast error of 200 basis points by early 2026. The authors conclude AI-related optimism cannot explain the recent surge in long-term yields. AlphaGen read: the note reflects the authors' views, not the Board's, and rests on a 1990–2019 sample dominated by the late-1990s tech boom.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, FEDS Notes

items.headline: Core PCE prices up 3.1% from a year earlier in September, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's core PCE price index (excluding food and energy) was 130.902 in September versus 126.940 in September 2025, a 3.1% year-over-year rise by AlphaGen's calculation. August's 130.489 against 126.646 a year earlier works out to 3.0%. AlphaGen read: the year-over-year pace edged up a tenth, which keeps the Fed's preferred inflation gauge above its 2% target.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (BEA data)

items.headline: Payroll jobs total 159.29M in October, 885,000 above a year earlier, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's total nonfarm payrolls series stood at 159,293 thousand in October 2026, versus 158,408 thousand in October 2025, a gain of 885 thousand or 0.56% (AlphaGen calculations). Since April's 158,798 thousand the level has risen 495 thousand. AlphaGen read: job growth over the past year has been modest in level terms, consistent with an unemployment rate that has stayed in a narrow band.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (BLS data)

items.headline: October permits of 1.295M ran 14,000 below starts of 1.309M, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's Census-sourced series show housing starts at 1,309 thousand and building permits at 1,295 thousand, both seasonally adjusted annual rates, for October 2026. Permits were 14 thousand below starts, or about 99% of them (AlphaGen calculations). AlphaGen read: permits lead construction, so a reading below starts suggests no further build-up in the pipeline.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Census data)

items.headline: EIA lifts end-November gas storage forecast by almost 70 Bcf after warm start
items.take: EIA said on Nov. 10 that it expects almost 70 billion cubic feet more natural gas in U.S. storage at the end of November than it forecast in October, citing a warm start to the month. In its November Short-Term Energy Outlook, it forecasts the Henry Hub spot price averaging $2.87 per MMBtu from November through March, 16% lower than the October forecast for that period. Milder early-winter weather is feeding straight into the gas price outlook.
items.source_name: EIA press release (Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA raises 2027 gasoline forecast to $3.73/gal from $3.56 on tight fuel supply
items.take: EIA's November STEO forecasts U.S. retail gasoline at $3.73 per gallon in 2027, up from $3.56 in its October forecast, a rise of 17 cents. EIA says refined-fuel supplies are expected to stay tight through 2027, and still forecasts both gasoline and diesel to fall in 2027. Its table puts 2026 gasoline at $3.89 against $3.10 in 2025.
items.source_name: EIA press release (Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: U.S. power generation on track for a record near 4,390 billion kWh in 2026
items.take: EIA's November STEO expects power-sector generation of almost 4,390 billion kilowatthours in 2026, a record and 2.7% above 2025. EIA expects most generation growth over the forecast period to come from utility-scale solar, with solar's share of U.S. generation going from 8% in 2026 to 10% in 2027. Rising power demand is now a core part of the energy outlook rather than a side note.
items.source_name: EIA press release (Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: U.S. crude stocks at lowest October level since 2014; 2027 output seen at 14.3M b/d
items.take: EIA says U.S. commercial crude oil inventories fell to their lowest October level since 2014. It expects inventories to rise in 2027 as net imports increase and U.S. crude production reaches a record 14.3 million barrels per day, up from 13.9 million in 2026. EIA's table puts Brent at $97 per barrel for 2026 and $86 for 2027, so the outlook is for a supply cushion rebuilding only gradually.
items.source_name: EIA press release (Nov. 10, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: Southwest hydropower hit record lows this summer, 19% below a year earlier
items.take: EIA reported on Nov. 13 that prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin led to record-low hydropower generation this summer in the Southwestern electricity supply region (Arizona, New Mexico, and small parts of Nevada and California). Generation from April through August 2026 was 19% lower than the same period last year and 28% lower than the 10-year average, per Form EIA-923 data. Drought is now a direct input to regional power supply, not just a water story.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy (Nov. 13, 2026)

items.headline: EUR/USD at 1.1034 on Nov. 13 is the lowest in a year of daily FRED readings
items.take: FRED shows the euro at $1.1034 on Nov. 13, below every daily observation since Nov. 13, 2025, when it was $1.1649. That is a decline of about 5.3% over the 12 months. The euro-dollar rate has sat near its year low alongside the broad dollar index's trailing-year high, a combination that points to broad dollar strength rather than a single-currency story.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DEXUSEU)

items.headline: Brent at $92.94 on Nov. 17 sits 33% below its April 7 peak of $138.21
items.take: FRED shows Brent crude at $92.94 per barrel on Nov. 17. Over the trailing year of daily readings, it peaked at $138.21 on April 7, 2026 and bottomed at $59.93 on Dec. 16, 2025. Today's reading is about 32.8% below the peak and $33.01 above the trough, so the market sits well inside that range, not at either end.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DCOILBRENTEU)

items.headline: Retail sales $748.2B in October, up 6.8% from $700.4B a year earlier, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's advance retail and food services series shows $748.2B in October 2026 versus $700.4B in October 2025, a gain of $47.8B or 6.8% in nominal terms. The series is not adjusted for price changes, and headline CPI is running at roughly 4% over 12 months by FRED's index, so a large share of the nominal gain is prices.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (RSAFS)

items.headline: 2-year Treasury at 4.76% on Nov. 19, 16 bp under its Sept. 28 high of 4.92%
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.76% on Nov. 19. Across the trailing year of daily data it ranged from 3.38% on Feb. 27, 2026 to 4.92% on Sept. 28, 2026, putting the latest reading 138 basis points above the low and 16 basis points below the high. With the fed funds effective rate at 3.88%, the 2-year remains well above where policy is today.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS2)

items.headline: USD/JPY at 159.93 on Nov. 13, 3.93 yen below its July 29 high of 163.86
items.take: FRED shows 159.93 yen per dollar on Nov. 13. The trailing-year high in the series was 163.86 on July 29, 2026, and the series stood at 154.40 on Nov. 13, 2025. The yen is therefore weaker than a year earlier by 5.53 yen, though it has recovered part of the way from its summer low.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DEXJPUS)

items.headline: Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% on Oct. 28, deliberations summary shows
items.take: The Bank of Canada's summary of Governing Council deliberations, published Nov. 10, says members weighed holding at 2.25% or raising to 2.5% and chose to raise, to reduce the risk that persistently high energy prices lead to broader price increases. It says the benchmark oil price was about US$35 per barrel higher than assumed in the July Report. AlphaGen read: the rationale is framed around energy pass-through rather than core inflation, which the Bank says remained near 2%.
items.source_name: Bank of Canada, Summary of Governing Council deliberations (Oct. 28, 2026 decision), published Nov. 10, 2026

items.headline: Bank of Canada sees CPI at 3½% by end-2026, back to 2% target by mid-2028
items.take: The Bank of Canada's Nov. 10 summary says CPI inflation was expected to rise to 3½% at the end of 2026 and stay above 3% through much of 2027 before declining to the 2% target by the middle of 2028; total inflation had been around 3% since April and CPI excluding gasoline was 2.2%. It also says members agreed there could be a need to raise the policy rate further but would decide one meeting at a time. AlphaGen read: the path implies the Bank expects the energy shock to take roughly two years to fully fade from headline inflation.
items.source_name: Bank of Canada, Summary of Governing Council deliberations (Oct. 28, 2026 decision), published Nov. 10, 2026

items.headline: BoJ's Takata: PPI up 7.1% y/y in October; he proposed a 1.5% rate at the October meeting
items.take: In a Nov. 16 speech, Bank of Japan Policy Board member Hajime Takata said the producer price index rose 7.1% year on year as of October 2026, that the Bank raised its policy rate to around 1.0% in June 2026 and to 1.25% in September, and that at the October meeting he proposed raising it to 1.5%, which he called solely his personal view. AlphaGen read: the speech is one board member's view, but it shows the debate at the BoJ has moved to the pace of further hikes.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, speech by Policy Board Member Hajime Takata, Nov. 16, 2026

items.headline: Fannie Mae's Nov. 12 forecast: 30-year mortgage rate averages 7.2% in Q4 2026, 2027
items.take: Fannie Mae's November 12, 2026 housing forecast shows the 30-year fixed rate averaging 7.2% in the fourth quarter of 2026 and in each quarter of 2027, for annual averages of 6.6% in 2026 and 7.2% in 2027; the rate forecasts are based on rates from Oct. 30. Its home price forecast (Q4/Q4) is 2.7% for 2026 and 0.6% for 2027. AlphaGen read: the forecast assumes no relief in borrowing costs through next year.
items.source_name: Fannie Mae Economic and Strategic Research, Housing Forecast, Nov. 12, 2026

items.headline: Fannie Mae forecasts 2026 total home sales of 4.655M, down 1.8%; starts 1.331M
items.take: Fannie Mae's Nov. 12 forecast shows total home sales of 4,655 thousand in 2026 (down 1.8% from 4,741 thousand in 2025) and 4,645 thousand in 2027, and total housing starts of 1,331 thousand in 2026 and 1,277 thousand in 2027 (down 4.1%). Multifamily starts are forecast at 434 thousand in 2026 and 391 thousand in 2027. AlphaGen read: the forecast has activity roughly flat next year, with multifamily doing the pulling back.
items.source_name: Fannie Mae Economic and Strategic Research, Housing Forecast, Nov. 12, 2026

items.headline: BLS: core CPI rose 0.3% in each of August, September and October
items.take: BLS reports the index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3% in October, as it did in September and August (seasonally adjusted). Compounded, three 0.3% gains come to about 0.9%, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: the monthly core pace has been steady across the three most recent reports, even as headline CPI swung between 0.6% in September and 0.4% in October.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: lodging away from home CPI rose 0.6% in October after 2.0% in September
items.take: BLS reports the lodging away from home index rose 0.6% in October after rising 2.0% the previous month, while the index for rent increased 0.2% and owners' equivalent rent 0.3%. The two lodging gains compound to about 2.6%, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: lodging prices added to shelter in the last two reports, while rent measures moved at a slower monthly pace.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: professional and business services added 70,000 jobs in October vs 15,000 average
items.take: BLS reports professional and business services employment rose 70,000 in October, well above its average monthly gain of 15,000 over the prior 12 months. Professional, scientific, and technical services added 33,000, administrative and support and waste management 28,000, and management of companies 9,000, which sum to the 70,000. AlphaGen read: the sector supplied 42% of October's 165,000 total payroll gain, by our calculation.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: October payrolls rose 165,000, versus a 48,000 average monthly gain over prior 12 months
items.take: BLS reports total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October, higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months, with the unemployment rate little changed at 4.1%. The October gain is 117,000 above that average, or about 3.4 times it, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: October was above from the 12-month pace, though BLS notes August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: new vehicles CPI rose 0.2% in October and 0.7% over 12 months
items.take: BLS reports the new vehicles index rose 0.2% in October after 0.2% in September, and 0.7% over the 12 months ended October (used cars and trucks fell 3.3% over the same span). The seasonally adjusted monthly changes from April to October (-0.2, -0.3, 0.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2) compound to about 0.3% by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: new-vehicle prices have edged higher while used-car prices have fallen.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: seven monthly CPI changes from April to October compound to about 2.2%
items.take: BLS reports the all-items CPI-U rose 0.4% in October after 0.6% in September; the seasonally adjusted monthly changes from April to October were 0.6, 0.5, -0.4, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.4. Compounded, that is about 2.2% over seven months, and about 1.4% over August through October, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded published figures. BLS did not collect October 2025 data, so it cannot publish a 12-month change for most October 2026 indexes. AlphaGen read: the late-summer pace has been faster than the spring-to-July average.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: food at home CPI rose 0.4% in October after -0.1% in September
items.take: BLS reports the food at home index rose 0.4% in October after -0.1% in September; the monthly path from April to October was 0.7, 0.1, 0.2, -0.1, 0.0, -0.1 and 0.4. Those seven changes compound to about 1.2%, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded figures. BLS said four of six major grocery group indexes rose in October and one fell. AlphaGen read: October's grocery gain was the largest since April's 0.7%.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: energy services CPI rose 0.6% in October; electricity +0.9%, natural gas -0.8%
items.take: BLS reports the energy services index rose 0.6% in October after 0.1% in September, with electricity up 0.9% and utility (piped) gas service down 0.8%. The monthly changes from April to October (1.6, 0.4, -0.7, 0.3, -0.4, 0.1, 0.6) compound to about 1.9%, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded figures. AlphaGen read: household energy-service costs have risen over the period even as natural gas service prices softened in October.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: Retail gasoline fell eight straight weeks to $3.805/gal from Sept. 21 peak of $4.478
items.take: FRED's weekly U.S. regular all-formulations retail gasoline price was $4.478 per gallon for the week of Sept. 21, 2026 and has fallen in each weekly observation since, to $3.805 for the week of Nov. 16. That is a decline of $0.673, or 15.0%, by AlphaGen's calculation. AlphaGen read: the weekly pump-price series has retraced a large part of the September run-up.
items.source_name: FRED (EIA series GASREGW)

items.headline: BLS: gasoline CPI up 37.4% over 12 months ended October, even after Oct. +1.0% monthly
items.take: BLS's October CPI table lists the gasoline (all types) index at +37.4% unadjusted over the 12 months ended October 2026, alongside seasonally adjusted monthly changes of +9.1% in September and +1.0% in October. AlphaGen read: the 12-month CPI gasoline change is far larger than the 24.3% year-on-year gap in FRED's weekly regular gasoline price for Nov. 16, because the two measures cover different dates and are built differently.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index news release (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS: apparel CPI rose 0.1% in October after 0.3% in September
items.take: BLS's October CPI table shows the apparel index up 0.1% in October, after +0.3% in September and unchanged in August, with a 0.6% rise in April and a 0.6% decline in June. Compounding the seven monthly changes from April through October gives about 0.8%, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded figures. AlphaGen read: apparel has been a small contributor to core goods prices this year.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index news release (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS: services less energy services outpaced core goods CPI from April to October
items.take: BLS's October CPI table shows services less energy services up 0.3% in October after 0.4% in September, and commodities less food and energy commodities up 0.2% after 0.3%. Compounding the seven monthly changes from April through October gives about 2.0% for services less energy services and 0.6% for core goods, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded figures. AlphaGen read: the core services index has run roughly three times as fast as core goods over the period.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index news release (October 2026)

items.headline: Retail and food services sales $748.2B in October, up 0.2% from September, FRED shows
items.take: FRED's seasonally adjusted retail and food services sales series (Census) shows $748,220 million for October 2026 versus $746,637 million for September, a gain of 0.21%, and 2.5% above July's $729,915 million, by AlphaGen's calculation. Sales have risen in each month since July's dip. AlphaGen read: the monthly pace slowed to 0.2% from larger gains in August and September.
items.source_name: FRED, Census Advance Retail Sales (RSAFS)

items.headline: BEA: September services exports $110.5B, imports $79.7B; surplus $30.9B
items.take: BEA and Census said exports of services rose $0.7 billion to $110.5 billion in September while imports of services rose $0.8 billion to $79.7 billion, leaving the services surplus at $30.9 billion, down less than $0.1 billion. Travel added $0.3 billion to exports and $0.5 billion to imports. AlphaGen read: services were a small, steady offset to the $135.9 billion goods deficit in the September report.
items.source_name: BEA, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: BEA: September goods exports rose $5.1B to $211.0B; capital goods +$3.8B
items.take: BEA and Census said exports of goods increased $5.1 billion to $211.0 billion in September. Capital goods rose $3.8 billion (computers +$1.3 billion, civilian aircraft +$0.7 billion) and foods, feeds and beverages rose $1.9 billion, with soybeans up $1.3 billion. Industrial supplies and materials fell $1.0 billion as nonmonetary gold dropped $3.4 billion and crude oil rose $1.2 billion. AlphaGen read: capital goods and food shipments, not industrial supplies, accounted for the monthly gain.
items.source_name: BEA, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: BEA: September goods imports $346.9B; pharmaceuticals +$2.9B
items.take: BEA and Census said imports of goods increased $4.4 billion to $346.9 billion in September. Consumer goods rose $2.4 billion, with pharmaceutical preparations up $2.9 billion, while industrial supplies and materials fell $3.7 billion, including nonmonetary gold (-$2.7 billion) and crude oil (-$1.3 billion). AlphaGen read: a pharmaceuticals rise and an industrial-supplies decline pulled in opposite directions within the monthly import total.
items.source_name: BEA, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: BEA: Sept. goods surpluses with Netherlands $7.7B, S. & Central America $6.2B
items.take: BEA and Census listed September goods surpluses (Census basis, seasonally adjusted) with the Netherlands ($7.7 billion), South and Central America ($6.2 billion), the United Kingdom ($3.0 billion), Hong Kong ($2.5 billion), Australia ($2.1 billion) and Brazil ($1.1 billion). The release lists the largest deficits with Mexico ($28.7 billion), Vietnam ($25.3 billion) and Taiwan ($21.9 billion). AlphaGen read: the surplus list is made up of European, Latin American and other partners, while the largest deficits are with Mexico and Asian partners.
items.source_name: BEA, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: BLS: October CPI gasoline +1.0% seasonally adjusted, -0.7% before adjustment
items.take: BLS said the gasoline index rose 1.0 percent in October after advancing 9.1 percent in September; before seasonal adjustment, gasoline prices decreased 0.7 percent. The electricity index rose 0.9 percent while the natural gas index fell 0.8 percent, and the overall energy index increased 0.7 percent after a 5.2-percent rise in September. AlphaGen read: seasonal adjustment turned a raw monthly gasoline decline into a reported increase.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index, October 2026

items.headline: BLS: manufacturing added 19,000 jobs in October, 101,000 since a December 2025 low
items.take: BLS said manufacturing employment continued to trend up in October (+19,000) and has increased by 101,000 since a recent low in December 2025. October gains came in computer and electronic product manufacturing (+7,000), machinery manufacturing (+4,000) and primary metal manufacturing (+4,000). AlphaGen read: manufacturing's 19,000 is a portion of the 165,000 total nonfarm payroll gain BLS reported for October.
items.source_name: BLS, Employment Situation

items.headline: BLS: transportation and warehousing added 25,000 jobs in October; couriers +17,000
items.take: BLS reported transportation and warehousing added 25,000 jobs in October, reflecting growth in couriers and messengers (+17,000) and air transportation (+4,000). The sector has added 104,000 jobs since a recent employment low in February, with couriers and messengers (+71,000) contributing most of the gain. AlphaGen read: the recovery in the sector is concentrated in delivery services rather than spread evenly across modes.
items.source_name: BLS, Employment Situation

items.headline: BLS: average hourly earnings rose 14 cents to $38.00 in October; up 3.1% in 12 months
items.take: BLS said average hourly earnings for all private nonfarm employees increased by 14 cents, or 0.4 percent, to $38.00 in October, and have risen 3.1 percent over the past 12 months. For production and nonsupervisory employees, earnings rose 12 cents, or 0.4 percent, to $32.75. AlphaGen read: the 3.1% annual pace in pay sits below the 3.8% 12-month PCE inflation rate Fed Governor Cook cited for October.
items.source_name: BLS, Employment Situation

items.headline: BLS: 6.0M people outside the labor force wanted a job in October; 448,000 discouraged
items.take: BLS said the number of people not in the labor force who currently want a job changed little at 6.0 million in October. The marginally attached numbered 1.6 million, and discouraged workers, a subset who believed no jobs were available for them, were little changed at 448,000. AlphaGen read: these slack measures sit alongside a 4.1% unemployment rate that BLS said has held in a 4.1%-to-4.3% range since March.
items.source_name: BLS, Employment Situation

items.headline: Cook: IMF analysis suggests advanced economies may capture a larger share of AI gains
items.take: Fed Governor Cook said in a Nov. 20 speech that recent IMF analysis suggests advanced economies may be positioned to capture a disproportionate share of global AI-driven productivity growth over the next decade, relative to developing economies. She asked where countries like Chile will land in that distribution and what will determine the outcome. AlphaGen read: Cook framed this as an open question, not a forecast, in remarks she delivered to a Central Bank of Chile conference.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, Governor Cook speech

items.headline: Fed total assets $6.741T on Nov. 18, $14.2B below Oct. 14 after a Nov. 11 high
items.take: FRED's WALCL series shows Federal Reserve total assets of $6,741,452 million on Nov. 18, versus $6,755,639 million on Oct. 14, a decline of $14.2 billion. Over that window the highest weekly reading was $6,758,867 million on Nov. 11. AlphaGen read: the balance sheet has drifted in a narrow band of roughly $17B across six weekly observations.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: EIA: U.S. refinery utilization averaged over 95% May–September, highest since 1998
items.take: EIA said in an Oct. 22 analysis that the U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. EIA attributed the high run rates to tight global product supplies that have boosted margins, particularly for diesel. AlphaGen read: this fits the refinery-yield shift toward distillate and jet fuel that EIA described in a separate Nov. 5 analysis.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy

items.headline: EIA: U.S. small-scale solar generation rose from 18,812 GWh to 92,979 GWh in a decade
items.take: EIA estimates U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar systems (under 1 megawatt) increased from 18,812 gigawatthours to 92,979 GWh over the last decade, according to its Oct. 16 analysis. By AlphaGen's calculation that is about 4.9 times the starting level, consistent with EIA's description of it as having quadrupled. California, Arizona, Texas and Florida are the top four states, with New York fifth.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy

items.headline: EIA: hybrids and EVs were 23% of new U.S. light-duty sales in 3Q26, from 24% a year earlier
items.take: EIA, citing Omdia data, said 23% of new light-duty vehicles sold in the U.S. in the third quarter of 2026 were hybrid, battery electric or plug-in hybrid, down slightly from 24% in 3Q25. Hybrid electric vehicles reached 16% of sales, while battery electric sales have stayed lower since the tax credit expired. EIA noted hybrid growth slowed as the average new-vehicle transaction price passed $50,000, the first time this year, according to Kelley Blue Book.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy

items.headline: EIA: PJM, ERCOT and SWPP all set peak hourly load records this summer
items.take: EIA reported on Oct. 15 that three regional transmission organizations (PJM, ERCOT and the Southwest Power Pool) set records for peak hourly load this past summer, based on Form EIA-930 data in its Hourly Electric Grid Monitor. The figures are the highest hourly load for a given day. AlphaGen read: record grid demand is the backdrop for EIA's separate projection of record U.S. electricity generation in 2026 and 2027.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy

items.headline: EIA: ISO New England wind generation up about 68% in first nine months of 2026
items.take: EIA said monthly wind generation in ISO New England averaged about 68% higher in the first nine months of 2026 than in the same period of 2025, based on Form EIA-930 data in its Oct. 14 analysis. AlphaGen read: the gain is a year-over-year comparison for a single grid region and should not be read as a national trend.
items.source_name: EIA, Today in Energy

items.headline: PayPal adds Brian J. Lee to board; strategy update set for Q4 earnings call
items.take: PayPal's Nov. 20 release says it appointed Brian J. Lee to its board of directors earlier that day; Lee spent six years as Chief Risk Officer at Goldman Sachs and has more than three decades of financial services experience. The company also said it will update investors on its three-year strategic plans on its fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call. AlphaGen read: the board addition arrives as the Chief Risk Officer, Aaron Webster, is departing, per the same release.
items.source_name: PayPal Holdings Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1

items.headline: Take-Two: Grand Theft Auto VI sold 32.5M units pre-release, company says
items.take: Rockstar Games' Nov. 20 release, furnished by Take-Two in an 8-K, says Grand Theft Auto VI sold 32.5 million units pre-release, which it calls a record across all platforms, and cites a Metacritic score of 99. The $3.79 billion day-one retail sales figure is a company estimate through the end of day Nov. 19, worldwide. AlphaGen read: these are company-reported launch metrics, not audited results; revenue recognition will show up in Take-Two's own quarterly filings.
items.source_name: Take-Two Interactive Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1

items.headline: Existing home sales 3.75M in October, down 5.5% from September and 8.8% from a year ago
items.take: FRED's existing home sales series shows 3,750,000 for October 2026, versus 3,970,000 in September, a drop of 220,000 or 5.5%, and 4,110,000 in October 2025, a decline of 8.8%. October is the lowest of the 13 monthly readings from October 2025, a span that ran from 3.75 million to 4.27 million. AlphaGen read: the 30-year mortgage rate was 7.28% on Nov. 19, and the latest sales reading came in at the bottom of its recent range.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Existing Home Sales)

items.headline: 5-year breakeven inflation rate 2.18% on Nov. 20, down 0.12 point in a week
items.take: FRED shows the 5-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.18% on Nov. 20, down 0.04 point from 2.22% on Nov. 19 and 0.12 point below 2.30% on Nov. 13. The 10-year breakeven was 2.15% on Nov. 20. AlphaGen read: the 5-year measure remains 0.03 point above the 10-year, so the market-implied inflation path over the nearer term still sits slightly higher.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T5YIE)

items.headline: EIA: U.S. crude imports from Venezuela hit 701,000 b/d in July, most since May 2017
items.take: EIA's Petroleum Supply Monthly shows U.S. crude oil imports from Venezuela averaged 701,000 barrels per day in July 2026, the most since May 2017, before easing to 655,000 b/d in August. That is a fall of 46,000 b/d month over month. AlphaGen read: this is a volume series, so it describes where U.S. refiners sourced barrels, not where prices are headed.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: Chart Industries June 30 total assets $9,868.4M; goodwill $3,061.0M, intangibles $2,411.4M
items.take: The Chart statements in Baker Hughes' latest 8-K show total assets of $9,868.4 million at June 30, 2026 versus $9,806.4 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of $62.0 million. Goodwill was $3,061.0 million (from $3,067.6 million) and identifiable intangible assets, net, were $2,411.4 million (from $2,511.7 million), so goodwill and intangibles together made up $5,472.4 million of the total. AlphaGen read: these are pre-closing Chart balances under Chart's own accounting policies, not Baker Hughes' combined figures.
items.source_name: Baker Hughes Form 8-K (Chart Industries unaudited financial statements)

items.headline: Chart Industries long-term debt rose to $3,859.1M at June 30 as cash fell to $309.1M
items.take: Chart's unaudited balance sheet in Baker Hughes' 8-K shows long-term debt of $3,859.1 million at June 30, 2026 versus $3,565.0 million at December 31, 2025, up $294.1 million, while cash and cash equivalents were $309.1 million versus $366.0 million. Total liabilities were $6,541.6 million versus $6,430.7 million, and total equity including noncontrolling interests was $3,326.8 million versus $3,375.7 million. AlphaGen read: the half-year balance sheet moved toward more debt and less cash before Baker Hughes completed the acquisition on July 16, 2026.
items.source_name: Baker Hughes Form 8-K (Chart Industries unaudited financial statements)

items.headline: Chart Industries June 30: receivables $853.6M, inventories $621.0M, unbilled revenue $1,078.0M
items.take: In the Chart statements Baker Hughes filed on Form 8-K, accounts receivable, net, were $853.6 million at June 30, 2026 versus $782.1 million at year-end 2025, inventories, net, were $621.0 million versus $572.3 million, and unbilled contract revenue was $1,078.0 million versus $986.4 million. Accounts payable fell to $1,109.4 million from $1,236.5 million. AlphaGen read: operating assets grew while payables shrank, which is consistent with more cash being tied up in working capital over the half-year.
items.source_name: Baker Hughes Form 8-K (Chart Industries unaudited financial statements)

items.headline: Fed H.8: bank assets $26,125.8B in week ended Nov. 11, up $62.1B
items.take: The Fed's H.8 release of Nov. 20 shows commercial bank total assets (not seasonally adjusted) of $26,125.8 billion in the week ending Nov. 11, versus $26,063.7 billion in the week ending Nov. 4, a $62.1 billion rise. Deposits were $19,830.0 billion, up $8.0 billion, and loans and leases in bank credit were $14,251.0 billion, up $18.5 billion. AlphaGen read: balance-sheet growth in the week came mostly from assets other than loans, since loans explained less than a third of the rise.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States, Nov. 20, 2026

items.headline: Fed H.8: October bank loans $14.20T, 7.9% above a year earlier
items.take: H.8 Table 3 shows October 2026 commercial bank loans and leases in bank credit at $14,198.2 billion versus $13,161.7 billion in October 2025, a 7.9 percent increase by AlphaGen's calculation. Deposits were $19,738.8 billion versus $18,419.2 billion (up 7.2 percent) and total assets $26,009.5 billion versus $24,407.0 billion (up 6.6 percent), all not seasonally adjusted. AlphaGen read: loans grew faster than deposits over the year, which pushes the loan-to-deposit ratio higher.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States, Nov. 20, 2026

items.headline: Fed H.8: October assets grew at 10.1% annual rate; C&I loans 11.7%
items.take: H.8 Table 1 reports October percent changes, break adjusted and seasonally adjusted at annual rates: total assets 10.1 percent, deposits 9.6 percent, loans and leases in bank credit 8.9 percent, bank credit 6.5 percent, and commercial and industrial loans 11.7 percent. The Fed also noted that domestically chartered banks divested $6.8 billion in assets and liabilities to nonbank institutions in the week ending Nov. 4. AlphaGen read: commercial and industrial lending was the fastest-growing of the loan lines the Fed highlights.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States, Nov. 20, 2026

items.headline: CPI: shelter rose 0.3% in October, over 30% of the all-items increase
items.take: BLS says the shelter index rose 0.3 percent in October after rising 0.4 percent in September, and accounted for over thirty percent of the monthly all-items increase of 0.4 percent. Within shelter, owners' equivalent rent rose 0.3 percent, rent 0.2 percent and lodging away from home 0.6 percent after a 2.0 percent rise the prior month. AlphaGen read: shelter remained a steady contributor, while lodging's 0.6 percent rise was smaller than September's 2.0 percent gain.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: CPI: shelter up about 1.0% over Aug-Oct; 2.1% compounded since April
items.take: BLS monthly shelter changes were 0.6, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.3 percent from April through October; AlphaGen compounds these to about 2.1 percent over seven months and about 1.0 percent over August to October. Services less energy services followed a similar path (0.5, 0.3, 0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.3), also near 1.0 percent over the last three months. AlphaGen read: the three-month pace is roughly 4 percent annualized, built from rounded monthly figures.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: BEA: U.S. parents of multinationals were 21.7% of private employment in 2024
items.take: BEA says U.S. parents accounted for 21.7 percent of total private industry employment in 2024, down from 21.9 percent in 2023, while their share of U.S. private-industry value added rose to 21.8 percent from 21.2 percent. U.S. parents' employment increased 0.1 percent to 29.9 million workers. AlphaGen read: the multinational parents' share of U.S. output grew even as their share of U.S. jobs slipped.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Activities of U.S. Multinational Enterprises, 2024

items.headline: BEA: foreign affiliates of U.S. multinationals employed 14.3M in 2024, up 2.7%
items.take: BEA reports employment abroad by foreign affiliates of U.S. multinationals rose 2.7 percent to 14.3 million workers in 2024 and was largest in India, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. Foreign affiliate value added increased 6.5 percent to $1.8 trillion, largest in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and Canada. AlphaGen read: the countries leading affiliate employment differ from those leading affiliate value added.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Activities of U.S. Multinational Enterprises, 2024

items.headline: BLS: unemployment rate has held between 4.1% and 4.3% since March
items.take: BLS says the October unemployment rate was 4.1 percent and the number of unemployed people was 7.1 million, both little changed, and that the rate has stayed in a narrow range of 4.1 percent to 4.3 percent since March. Payrolls rose by 165,000 in October versus an average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months. AlphaGen read: a steady jobless rate alongside faster October hiring is what the Fed has in front of it before its December meeting.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary, October 2026

items.headline: EIA: weekly gas injections ranged from 108 Bcf in June to 15 Bcf in August
items.take: EIA says weekly natural gas injections in the 2026 refill season ranged from 108 Bcf in early June to 15 Bcf in late August, and mild temperatures in the final weeks of the season led to above-normal injections. Net injections were 2 Bcf below the five-year average, but stocks ended the season at 3,810 Bcf, almost 2 percent above it. AlphaGen read: a large early-season cushion meant smaller injections were enough to finish above normal.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: CPI: used cars and trucks fell 1.2% in October; down 3.3% over 12 months
items.take: BLS says the used cars and trucks index declined 1.2% in October after rising 0.7% in September, and its table shows a 3.3% decline over the 12 months ended October 2026. The new vehicles index rose 0.2% in October and 0.7% over 12 months. AlphaGen read: used vehicles and new vehicles moved in opposite directions in October.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: CPI all items rose about 2.2% from March to October; core about 1.7%
items.take: BLS's Table A shows seasonally adjusted all-items changes of 0.6, 0.5, -0.4, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.4% for April through October 2026, and core (less food and energy) changes of 0.4, 0.2, 0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.3 and 0.3%. AlphaGen compounded those published, rounded monthly rates: roughly 2.2% for all items and 1.7% for core over the seven months. AlphaGen read: the headline path is driven by energy, which swung from -5.7% in June to +5.2% in September.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: CPI: medical care commodities rose 0.5% in October after a 0.7% decline
items.take: BLS's Table A shows the medical care commodities index up 0.5% in October after falling 0.7% in September; BLS marks that line as not seasonally adjusted. The prescription drugs index rose 0.3% in October, and the medical care index overall rose 0.3% after a 0.1% rise in September. AlphaGen read: medical care commodities swung from a decline to a gain between September and October.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate rose 0.17 point to 7.28% on Nov. 19 after four weekly declines
items.take: FRED's Freddie Mac series shows the 30-year fixed rate at 7.40% on Oct. 15, then 7.32%, 7.24%, 7.18% and 7.11% through Nov. 12, before rising to 7.28% on Nov. 19. That is a 0.29-point fall over four weeks followed by a 0.17-point rebound, still below the 7.40% start of the window. AlphaGen read: one weekly uptick does not erase most of the October-November decline.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Freddie Mac, MORTGAGE30US)

items.headline: Henry Hub spot gas hit $3.26 on Nov. 13, the high of a six-day FRED window
items.take: FRED's Henry Hub series shows $3.00 per million Btu on Nov. 10, 11 and 12, $3.26 on Nov. 13, $3.20 on Nov. 16 and $3.10 on Nov. 17. The Nov. 13 print was $0.26 above the prior day, and the Nov. 17 figure was $0.16 below that peak. AlphaGen read: the Nov. 17 spot price remained above the $3.00 recorded earlier in the window.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Henry Hub Natural Gas Spot Price, DHHNGSP)

items.headline: EIA: refiners cut gasoline yields in 2026 to make more distillate and jet fuel
items.take: EIA says particularly high refinery margins for distillate fuel oil and jet fuel have contributed to shifts in refinery yields in 2026. Data through August 2026 in its Petroleum Supply Monthly show gasoline yields have decreased significantly this year as production moved to distillate and jet fuel. AlphaGen read: the product mix, not just crude supply, is shaping what consumers and businesses pay for fuels.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy (Nov. 5, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: global refinery inputs fell 4.8M b/d in Q2 2026, then rebounded 1.8M in Q3
items.take: EIA, citing Kpler data, says global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (6%) in the second quarter of 2026 after conflict began in the Middle East in late February. Throughput then rose by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows. AlphaGen read: net of the rebound, inputs remained about 3.0 million b/d below the pre-decline level (AlphaGen calculation).
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy (Nov. 3, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: over 16% of new 2026 utility-scale solar is built with co-located batteries
items.take: As of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017, EIA reports, citing operator filings in its EIA-860M survey. That is eight times the 2017 share (AlphaGen calculation). AlphaGen read: pairing storage with solar is moving from niche to a routine part of new builds.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy (Oct. 30, 2026)

items.headline: EIA: Colombia leans more on LNG imports as domestic gas output keeps falling
items.take: EIA says Colombia is importing more liquefied natural gas as domestic production continues to fall. A potential drought this fall and winter could limit hydroelectric generation and boost demand for natural gas power generation, and the government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought from an expected strong El Niño. AlphaGen read: weather-driven power demand in import-reliant markets is another source of LNG demand.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy (Oct. 29, 2026)

items.headline: BLS: November Real Earnings release scheduled for Dec. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS lists the Real Earnings news release for November 2026 for Thursday, December 10, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. (ET). The October release, issued Nov. 10, showed real average hourly earnings for all employees unchanged. AlphaGen read: the next print will show whether pay growth and CPI keep moving together.
items.source_name: BLS, Real Earnings news release (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS: no over-the-year real earnings comparison for October due to 2025 data gap
items.take: BLS says it could not collect the relevant Consumer Price Index data for the October 2025 reference period because of a lapse in appropriations in late 2025, so over-the-year comparisons from October 2025 to October 2026 are not available. The release usually includes that analysis. AlphaGen read: monthly changes are the usable real-pay read this month.
items.source_name: BLS, Real Earnings news release (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS: production workers' pay up 0.4% vs CPI-W up 0.3% in October
items.take: BLS reports average hourly earnings for production and nonsupervisory employees rose 0.4 percent in October, against a 0.3 percent increase in CPI-W, leaving real hourly earnings up 0.1 percent. For all employees, pay and CPI-U both rose 0.4 percent. AlphaGen read: the one-tenth gap for production workers is the difference between the two price gauges.
items.source_name: BLS, Real Earnings news release (October 2026)

items.headline: BEA: Q3 real GDP 3.4% annualized, 0.8% at a quarterly rate; current-dollar GDP 5.6%
items.take: BEA's advance estimate has real GDP up 3.4 percent at an annual rate in the third quarter (0.8 percent at a quarterly rate), after 2.2 percent in the second quarter. Current-dollar GDP rose 5.6 percent at an annual rate. AlphaGen read: the gap between nominal and real growth reflects price changes; the second estimate is due Nov. 25.
items.source_name: BEA, GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026

items.headline: Trade: year-to-date deficit down $92.4B, 12.2%, as exports rise 11.6%
items.take: BEA and Census report the goods and services deficit through September is down $92.4 billion, or 12.2 percent, from the same period in 2025. Year to date, exports increased $297.3 billion, or 11.6 percent, and imports increased $204.9 billion, or 6.2 percent. AlphaGen read: the narrower year-to-date gap comes from exports growing faster in percentage terms than imports.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: Real goods deficit up 3.0% to $119.5B in September vs 2.2% nominal rise
items.take: BEA's Census-basis real goods deficit in 2017 dollars increased $3.5 billion, or 3.0 percent, to $119.5 billion in September, versus a 2.2 percent increase in the nominal deficit. Real exports of goods rose 0.1 percent to $152.2 billion and real imports rose 1.4 percent to $271.6 billion. AlphaGen read: after adjusting for prices, imports outpaced exports in volume terms.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: Trade: gold swings trimmed both September exports and imports
items.take: BEA reports nonmonetary gold exports decreased $3.4 billion in September, while nonmonetary gold imports decreased $2.7 billion. Crude oil exports rose $1.2 billion and crude oil imports fell $1.3 billion. AlphaGen read: gold lowered both sides of the ledger, so they should be netted out when reading the $105.0 billion deficit.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: September imports: computers up $7.6B, capital goods up $11.6B, semiconductors down $1.2B
items.take: BEA reports imports of goods rose $4.4 billion to $346.9 billion in September, with capital goods up $11.6 billion, including computers up $7.6 billion and computer accessories up $5.7 billion. Semiconductors decreased $1.2 billion, and industrial supplies and materials decreased $3.7 billion. AlphaGen read: the import increase was concentrated in computing equipment.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: BLS PPI: trade services margins fell 0.2% in October; machinery wholesaling down 4.2%
items.take: BLS's October Producer Price Index (released Nov. 13) shows margins for final demand trade services decreased 0.2%, and margins for machinery and vehicle wholesaling fell 4.2%. BLS's table puts trade services at +2.1% in September (revised). AlphaGen read: trade margins went from +2.1% to -0.2% in a month when transportation and warehousing prices rose 2.0%.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index Summary (October 2026)

items.headline: PPI services: outpatient care, lodging up in October; airline services, software down
items.take: BLS's October PPI says final demand services rose 0.2%, the fifth consecutive advance. Among product indexes that moved higher were hospital outpatient care, traveler accommodation services, health, beauty and optical goods retailing, and fuels and lubricants retailing. Prices for system software publishing and for airline passenger services declined. AlphaGen read: BLS attributes over 80% of the services increase to truck freight, which rose 3.9%.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index Summary (October 2026)

items.headline: PPI goods detail: vegetables, chickens up in October; pork and passenger cars down
items.take: In BLS's October PPI, the final demand goods index rose 0.5%. Within it, indexes for fresh and dry vegetables, gas fuels, aeronautical, nautical and navigational instruments, jet fuel and processed young chickens moved higher, while the indexes for pork and for passenger cars declined. AlphaGen read: food and fuel items sat on both sides of the ledger, and final demand foods as a group rose 1.3%.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index Summary (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS to rename three CPI index titles with January 2027 data on Feb. 11, 2027
items.take: BLS says that with the publication of January 2027 CPI data on February 11, 2027, several index titles will change: "wireless telephone services" becomes "wireless telephone service", "physicians' services" becomes "physician services", and "music instruments and accessories" becomes "music instruments and accessories including instrument rentals." AlphaGen read: this is a title change in BLS's notice, which does not itself describe any change to index figures.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index Summary (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS: Aug. payrolls revised up to +186,000, Sept. to +60,000; 84,000 combined
items.take: BLS's October Employment Situation (released Nov. 6) revised August nonfarm payroll growth up by 53,000, from +133,000 to +186,000, and September up by 31,000, from +29,000 to +60,000. With the revisions, employment in August and September combined is 84,000 higher than previously reported. AlphaGen read: the two earlier months now look stronger than first published, alongside October's +165,000.
items.source_name: BLS, Employment Situation Summary (October 2026)

items.headline: CPI electricity index up 0.9% in October, after +0.2% in September
items.take: BLS's October CPI (released Nov. 10) shows the electricity index rose 0.9% in October on a seasonally adjusted basis, after +0.2% in September and -0.2% in August; the table lists +2.1% for April. Compounding the seven monthly changes from April through October gives about 2.7%, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded figures. AlphaGen read: electricity rose on net from April through October even as the piped natural gas index fell 0.8% in October.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: CPI energy index up 0.7% in October after +5.2% in September
items.take: BLS reports the October CPI energy index rose 0.7% on a seasonally adjusted basis after rising 5.2% in September; the table shows +2.1% for August, -1.5% for July and -5.7% for June. Compounding August through October gives about 8.2%, by AlphaGen's calculation from rounded monthly figures. AlphaGen read: the energy index has climbed for three straight months after falling in June and July.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: CPI medical care services up 0.3% in October for a second month
items.take: BLS's October CPI table shows medical care services rose 0.3% in October and 0.3% in September, after -0.2% in August and +0.6% in July. The release says the overall medical care index rose 0.3% in October after +0.1% in September, with hospital services up 0.8% and physicians' services up 0.4%. AlphaGen read: compounding July through October gives about 1.0% for medical care services, by our calculation from rounded figures.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: Treasury refunding table: Nov. 2-year $69B, 5-year $70B, 7-year $44B notes
items.take: Treasury's Nov. 4 refunding statement lists anticipated November auction sizes of $69 billion for 2-year notes, $70 billion for 5-year notes and $44 billion for 7-year notes, the same sizes shown for August. It said Treasury "anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the next several quarters." AlphaGen read: the sizes are unchanged, so the coming end-of-month supply is a repeat of the prior quarter.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Quarterly Refunding Statement (Nov. 4, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury to make 7-year note a quarterly new issue from March 2027
items.take: Treasury plans to convert the 7-year note from a monthly new issue to a quarterly new issue with two reopenings, similar to the 10-year note. New issues will come in March, June, September and December, with reopenings in the following two months; the change starts with the March 2027 new issue, reopened in April and May. AlphaGen read: this is a change to the calendar, not to the coupon sizes Treasury said it expects to keep.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Quarterly Refunding Statement (Nov. 4, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury plans up to $70B liquidity buybacks, $25B cash-management buybacks this quarter
items.take: Treasury said it anticipates purchasing up to $70 billion in off-the-run securities for liquidity support and up to $25 billion in the 1-month to 2-year bucket for cash management over the upcoming quarter. It expects to reduce shorter-dated bill auction sizes during December and to increase auction sizes across the bill curve in January on seasonal fiscal outflows. AlphaGen read: the bill path is seasonal, with smaller sizes in December and larger ones in January.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Quarterly Refunding Statement (Nov. 4, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury assumes $850B end-December cash; TGA could peak near $1.025T
items.take: Treasury said it is assuming an $850 billion cash balance at the end of December, and that the Treasury General Account could peak at $1.025 trillion (plus or minus $50 billion) in late November and late January. It called these figures consistent with its cash balance policy and set the next refunding announcement for Wednesday, Feb. 3, 2027. AlphaGen read: a TGA near $1 trillion matters for bank reserves, which the Fed tracks weekly.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury, Quarterly Refunding Statement (Nov. 4, 2026)

items.headline: Week to Nov. 19: 2-year yield down 0.10 point, high-yield spread up 0.32
items.take: FRED data show the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.76% on Nov. 19 versus 4.86% on Nov. 12 (down 0.10 point), and the 10-year at 5.04% versus 5.10% (down 0.06 point). Over the same week the high-yield spread widened to 3.52 points from 3.20 (up 0.32). AlphaGen read: yields and credit spreads moved in opposite directions over the week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate 7.28% vs 6.26% a year ago; one-year range 5.98% to 7.40%
items.take: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.28% in the week of Nov. 19, up from 6.26% in the week of Nov. 20, 2025. Over the past year the weekly rate ranged from 5.98% (Feb. 26, 2026) to 7.40% (Oct. 8, 2026). AlphaGen read: the rate is 1.02 points above its year-ago level, though still 0.12 point below the October peak.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac via FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

items.headline: Treasury yields on Nov. 19 sit 0.65 to 1.18 points above a year earlier
items.take: On Nov. 19, the 2-year yield was 4.76% (3.58% a year earlier, +1.18 points), the 10-year 5.04% (4.13%, +0.91) and the 30-year 5.40% (4.75%, +0.65). Each remains below its one-year high: 4.92% on Sept. 28, 5.31% on Oct. 5 and 5.67% on Oct. 7, respectively. AlphaGen read: the largest year-on-year rise is at the short end, which has flattened the curve compared with a year ago.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: 3-month Treasury yield 4.34% on Nov. 19, matching its one-year high, vs 3.95 a year ago
items.take: The 3-month constant-maturity Treasury yield was 4.34% on Nov. 19, equal to the Nov. 16 reading and the highest in the past 12 months of FRED data, compared with 3.95% on Nov. 19, 2025 and a low of 3.62% on Dec. 18, 2025. The effective fed funds rate was 3.88% on Nov. 19. AlphaGen read: the bill yield sitting 0.46 point above fed funds means short-dated Treasuries yield more than the policy rate.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Fed broad dollar index 122.6503 on Nov. 13, highest since May 16, 2025
items.take: The Federal Reserve's nominal broad dollar index (trade-weighted, FRED series DTWEXBGS) stood at 122.6503 on Nov. 13, against 120.7725 a year earlier and a one-year low of 117.4396 on Jan. 29, 2026. The last higher reading was 123.0737 on May 16, 2025. AlphaGen read: the index is 5.2 points above its January low, a firmer dollar against trading partners.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: High-yield spread 3.52 points on Nov. 19, highest since May 9, 2025
items.take: FRED's ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread was 3.52 percentage points on Nov. 19, versus 3.17 a year earlier on Nov. 19, 2025, and a low of 2.60 on Aug. 28, 2026. The last higher reading was 3.53 on May 9, 2025. AlphaGen read: the gap to Treasuries has widened about 0.9 point since late August, a sign lenders are asking more to hold lower-rated corporate debt.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: BEA: Q3 gross domestic purchases prices up 3.0% annualized, after 5.6% in Q2
items.take: BEA's advance estimate (released Oct. 29) shows the price index for gross domestic purchases increased 3.0% at an annual rate in the third quarter, compared with 5.6% in the second. The PCE price index rose 2.1%, versus 5.0%, and PCE excluding food and energy rose 2.5%, versus 3.3%. AlphaGen read: BEA's second estimate, due Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. EST, will show whether these price measures are revised.
items.source_name: BEA GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026

items.headline: BEA: Q3 real final sales to private domestic purchasers up 4.9%, from 4.6% in Q2
items.take: BEA's advance estimate (released Oct. 29) put real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, up 4.9% at an annual rate in the third quarter, versus 4.6% in the second. Real GDP rose 3.4% and current-dollar GDP 5.6%. AlphaGen read: private domestic demand grew faster than headline GDP, which BEA says was partly offset by a decrease in exports and an increase in imports.
items.source_name: BEA GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026

items.headline: CPI-U index level 337.511 in October; CPI-W 331.147, C-CPI-U up 0.2% unadjusted
items.take: BLS reported the October CPI-U at 337.511 (1982-84=100), up 0.2% for the month before seasonal adjustment, and the CPI-W at 331.147, up 0.1% before seasonal adjustment. The chained C-CPI-U rose 0.2% on a not seasonally adjusted basis, and BLS notes its indexes for the past 10 to 12 months are subject to revision. AlphaGen read: the seasonally adjusted all-items change was +0.4%, so the unadjusted gain was smaller.
items.source_name: BLS Consumer Price Index, October 2026

items.headline: CPI: food away from home +0.5% in October; full service +0.7%, limited +0.4%
items.take: BLS's October CPI release (Nov. 10) shows the food away from home index rose 0.5% after +0.2% in September; full service meals rose 0.7% and limited service meals 0.4%. The overall food index rose 0.5% after being unchanged in September, with food at home up 0.4%. AlphaGen read: restaurant prices rose faster than grocery prices in the month.
items.source_name: BLS Consumer Price Index, October 2026

items.headline: CPI: transportation services up 0.8% in October, after +0.6% in September
items.take: BLS's October CPI release (Nov. 10) shows the transportation services index rose 0.8% on a seasonally adjusted basis, after +0.6% in September and +0.5% in August. The release also lists the airline fares index among core indexes that increased in October. AlphaGen read: transportation services have risen in each of the last three months in the release's table, a category to watch alongside shelter in the core reading.
items.source_name: BLS Consumer Price Index, October 2026

items.headline: American Airlines: COO Seymour to step down Dec. 31; Gulbranson named COO Jan. 1
items.take: In a Form 8-K (Item 5.02) dated Nov. 20, American Airlines Group said David G. Seymour will cease serving as Chief Operating Officer on Dec. 31, 2026, and JonCarlo Gulbranson, 49, currently Senior Vice President, Operations, will become Executive Vice President, Chief Operations Officer effective Jan. 1, 2027. Seymour is expected to serve as a strategic advisor for up to three months at $25,000 per month. AlphaGen read: this updates our earlier alert-only note on the filing, which did not name the officers.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR, American Airlines Group Form 8-K

items.headline: BLS PPI: final demand up 0.3% in October; 6.5% over 12 months, most since Nov. 2022
items.take: BLS's October Producer Price Index (released Nov. 13) showed final demand rising 0.3% seasonally adjusted after a 1.4% rise in September. On an unadjusted basis the index rose 6.5% over the 12 months ended in October, the largest 12-month rise since 7.4% in November 2022. AlphaGen read: the monthly pace cooled sharply from September, while the year-over-year level stayed high.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS PPI: unprocessed intermediate goods fell 3.1% in October; crude petroleum down 10.3%
items.take: BLS said prices for unprocessed goods for intermediate demand fell 3.1% in October, the largest decline since a 6.6% drop in June, led by a 7.7% drop in unprocessed energy materials, including a 10.3% decrease in crude petroleum. Over the 12 months ended in October the index was still up 16.9%. AlphaGen read: the monthly drop sits alongside a very large year-over-year gain in raw-materials costs.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: BLS PPI: processed intermediate goods up 14.6% in 12 months, most since July 2022
items.take: BLS said prices for processed goods for intermediate demand advanced 0.4% in October, the third consecutive rise, and increased 14.6% over the 12 months ended in October, the largest 12-month rise since 17.2% in July 2022. More than 40% of the October advance traced to basic organic chemicals, up 3.9%. AlphaGen read: input costs further up the supply chain remain well above year-ago levels.
items.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Producer Price Index (October 2026)

items.headline: BB spread 2.10 points on Nov. 19, up 0.24 in a week; BBB 1.17, CCC-and-lower 13.61
items.take: FRED's ICE BofA option-adjusted spreads on Nov. 19 were 2.10 points for BB, 1.17 for BBB and 13.61 for CCC and lower, versus 1.86, 1.11 and 13.16 on Nov. 13. That is increases of 0.24, 0.06 and 0.45 point. AlphaGen read: the widening was larger in lower-rated tiers than in BBB over those four observations.
items.source_name: FRED, ICE BofA BB US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (BAMLH0A1HYBB)

items.headline: UK long-term government bond yield 5.34% in October, up 0.77 point from a year earlier
items.take: FRED's monthly long-term government bond yield series for the United Kingdom read 5.3393% in October 2026, up from 5.2421% in September, 4.9886% in August and 4.5721% in October 2025. That is 0.0972 point above September and 0.7672 point above a year earlier. AlphaGen read: the series has risen in each of the last three monthly readings.
items.source_name: FRED, Long-Term Government Bond Yields: 10-Year, United Kingdom (IRLTLT01GBM156N)

items.headline: SOFR 3.91% on Nov. 19, 0.03 point above the 3.88% effective fed funds rate
items.take: FRED shows the Secured Overnight Financing Rate at 3.91% on Nov. 19, up from 3.90% on Nov. 18, while the effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on both days. SOFR was 3.90% on Nov. 12 and 3.93% at its Nov. 16 reading. AlphaGen read: the two overnight benchmarks remained within 0.05 point of each other across the observations shown.
items.source_name: FRED, Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR)

items.headline: 2-year Treasury yield 4.76% on Nov. 19, 0.88 point above the 3.88% fed funds rate
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.76% on Nov. 19, versus an effective federal funds rate of 3.88%, a gap of 0.88 point. The 2-year yield was 4.86% on Nov. 12, when the effective rate was also 3.88%, a gap of 0.98 point. items.source_name: FRED, Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity (DGS2)

items.headline: BEA: outdoor recreation by industry led by arts/lodging/food at $179.5B, retail $166.5B
items.take: BEA said the arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation and food services group was the largest industry contributor to 2025 outdoor recreation value added at $179.5 billion (25.5%), ahead of retail trade at $166.5 billion (23.6%) and transportation and warehousing at $86.4 billion (12.3%). The largest state contributions in the first group were California ($23.5 billion), Florida ($23.4 billion) and New York ($11.6 billion). AlphaGen read: those three groups sum to $432.4 billion, about 61.4% of the sector's $704.2 billion.
items.source_name: BEA, Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

items.headline: BEA: RVing was $26.8B of outdoor recreation value added in 2025; Indiana led at $4.7B
items.take: BEA reported RVing was the second-largest conventional outdoor recreation activity nationally at $26.8 billion in 2025 current-dollar value added and the largest in 10 states, with Indiana ($4.7 billion), Texas ($2.6 billion) and California ($2.1 billion) the largest state contributions. Hunting/shooting/trapping was third at $15.1 billion, led by Texas ($1.8 billion). AlphaGen read: RVing's state footprint is concentrated differently from boating and fishing, with Indiana at the top.
items.source_name: BEA, Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

items.headline: BEA: supporting activities were 51.5% of outdoor recreation value added in 2025
items.take: BEA said supporting outdoor recreation, such as construction, travel and tourism, local trips and government expenditures, accounted for 51.5% of 2025 outdoor recreation value added, versus 51.7% in 2024. Conventional activities were 29.2% (29.1% in 2024) and other activities 19.3% (19.1%). AlphaGen read: the mix barely moved, with supporting spending still about half the sector.
items.source_name: BEA, Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate sat 1.88 points above 30-year Treasury yield on Nov. 19, from 1.68
items.take: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.28% in the week of Nov. 19, versus a 30-year Treasury constant-maturity yield of 5.40% that day, a gap of 1.88 percentage points. On Nov. 12 the rate was 7.11% against a 5.43% yield, a gap of 1.68 points, so the gap widened 0.20 point. AlphaGen read: the mortgage rate rose over the week while the long Treasury yield slipped, so the spread, not the Treasury market, drove the increase.
items.source_name: FRED, Freddie Mac 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average (MORTGAGE30US) and 30-Year Treasury (DGS30)

items.headline: BEA: outdoor recreation jobs rose in 43 states and DC in 2025; RI, KS, DC up 5.0%
items.take: BEA said outdoor recreation employment increased in 43 states and the District of Columbia in 2025, with changes ranging from 5.0% in Rhode Island, Kansas and the District of Columbia to -1.1% in New Jersey and Alabama. Nationally, outdoor recreation employment rose 1.7% and compensation 4.6%. AlphaGen read: job growth in the sector was spread across most states, with only a few at the bottom of the range posting declines.
items.source_name: BEA, Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

items.headline: BEA: outdoor recreation is 6.1% of Hawaii's GDP vs 1.0% in DC; snow activities $7.8B
items.take: BEA reported outdoor recreation value added at 2.3% ($704.2 billion) of U.S. current-dollar GDP in 2025, ranging by state from 6.1% in Hawaii to 1.0% in the District of Columbia. Snow activities totaled $7.8 billion nationally, with Colorado ($1.8 billion), California ($735.7 million) and Utah ($640.1 million) the largest state contributions. AlphaGen read: the state share range shows how unevenly the sector's weight is spread across local economies.
items.source_name: BEA, Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

items.headline: Lagarde: acting late on Greece cost a six-quarter recession; last Frankfurt keynote
items.take: In her Nov. 20 keynote at the 36th Frankfurt European Banking Congress, ECB President Christine Lagarde said it was the eighth time she had spoken there as President and "it will sadly be the last." She said the scale of Greece's difficulties was clear long before Europe acted decisively, and that Europe paid a much higher price than if it had acted earlier, including a six-quarter recession. AlphaGen read: the speech frames slow-moving risks as the ones European institutions find hardest to act on early.
items.source_name: European Central Bank, Christine Lagarde: Acting in time

items.headline: Lagarde: over a third of euro area daily spending is online; ICC judges lost cards
items.take: Lagarde said cash plays a smaller role as spending moves online, where more than a third of day-to-day spending now takes place, and that judges of the International Criminal Court living in Europe, some of them European citizens, lost the use of their bank cards overnight. She cited the changed geopolitical climate and the shift online as reasons the ECB concluded Europe needed a digital equivalent of cash, the digital euro. AlphaGen read: the ECB is tying the digital euro case to payments dependence, not only to cash decline.
items.source_name: European Central Bank, Christine Lagarde: Acting in time

items.take: FRED shows the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.40% and the 2-year at 4.76% on Nov. 19, a gap of 0.64 percentage point. On Nov. 12 the yields were 5.43% and 4.86%, a gap of 0.57. items.take: FRED reports the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.28% for Nov. 19, up from 7.11% on Nov. 12. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.04% on Nov. 19 and 5.10% on Nov. 12, so the gap widened to 2.24 points from 2.01. items.headline: 2-year Treasury yield 0.85 point above SOFR on Nov. 19, from 0.96 on Nov. 12
items.take: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.76% and SOFR at 3.91% on Nov. 19, a gap of 0.85 percentage point. On Nov. 12 the 2-year was 4.86% and SOFR 3.90%, a gap of 0.96. AlphaGen read: the gap narrowed because the 2-year yield fell 0.10 point while SOFR moved up 0.01.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Fed calendar: Thanksgiving week releases shift; H.4.1 set for Fri. Nov. 27, 4:30 p.m.
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's November calendar lists Thursday, Nov. 26 as a Thanksgiving holiday and says the daily and weekly statistical releases scheduled for that day will be released on Friday, Nov. 27. The calendar lists H.4.1 (Factors Affecting Reserve Balances) at 4:30 p.m. and H.8 (Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks) at 4:15 p.m. that Friday. items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board

items.headline: BLS: October jobless rates lower in 3 states and DC, higher in 1, stable in 46
items.take: BLS reported on Nov. 20 that in October unemployment rates were lower in 3 states and the District of Columbia, higher in 1 state and stable in 46 states. Nonfarm payroll employment increased in 4 states and was essentially unchanged in 46 states and the District. AlphaGen read: the state map was mostly flat in October, with changes confined to a handful of states.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)

items.headline: BLS: total factor productivity rose in 7 of 19 major industries in 2025
items.take: BLS published its industry productivity release on Nov. 20, reporting that total factor productivity increased in 7 out of 19 major industries in 2025. AlphaGen read: that leaves 12 of the 19 industries without an increase, so the 2025 gains were not broad across the industries BLS covers.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)

items.headline: BLS: employers reported 2.4 million workplace injury and illness cases in 2025
items.take: BLS reported on Nov. 18 that employers reported 2.4 million injury and illness cases in 2025, down 3.0% from 2024. AlphaGen read: the count is an annual workplace-safety measure rather than a market series, and it is a decline from the 2024 level.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)

items.headline: BLS latest numbers: Q3 ECI +0.8%, Q3 productivity +3.6%, October jobless rate 4.1%
items.take: BLS's Latest Numbers panel, as of Nov. 20, lists the Employment Cost Index at +0.8% in Q3 2026, productivity at +3.6% in Q3 2026, the unemployment rate at 4.1% in October, and payroll employment at +165,000 (preliminary) in October. It also shows the October CPI at +0.4% and the October PPI for final demand at +0.3% (preliminary). AlphaGen read: the next jobs report is scheduled for Dec. 4 at 8:30 a.m. ET, per BLS.
items.source_name: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)

items.headline: Sept. goods deficits: Mexico $28.7B, Vietnam $25.3B, Taiwan $21.9B, China $17.9B
items.take: BEA and Census list September goods deficits, in billions of dollars, of $28.7 with Mexico, $25.3 with Vietnam, $21.9 with Taiwan and $17.9 with China (Census basis, seasonally adjusted). Together those four come to $93.8B. AlphaGen read: the four largest bilateral gaps in the release sit with Mexico and three Asian economies, with China fourth.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) / Census Bureau

items.headline: Sept. trade: Taiwan deficit up $3.6B to $21.9B; Canada's down $2.7B to $4.4B
items.take: The September deficit with Taiwan rose $3.6B to $21.9B as imports climbed $4.2B to $27.3B and exports rose $0.6B to $5.3B. The deficit with the European Union rose $3.2B to $14.2B (exports $39.0B, imports $53.2B), while the Canada deficit fell $2.7B to $4.4B as imports dropped $3.0B to $34.1B. AlphaGen read: Taiwan and the EU widened on import growth, while Canada narrowed because imports fell by more than exports.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) / Census Bureau

items.headline: BEA: Q3 federal spending rise reflects smaller Strategic Petroleum Reserve sales
items.take: BEA's advance Q3 GDP estimate says the increase in government spending was more than accounted for by federal spending, led by nondefense consumption. BEA attributes that pattern to crude oil sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which were smaller than in Q2; sales are deducted from government consumption expenditures. BEA adds that oil sold by the government shows up as an increase in other GDP components, so there is no direct effect on GDP. AlphaGen read: part of the federal spending swing is an accounting effect of the reserve-sale pace.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)

items.headline: BEA: Q3 consumer spending led by health care and food services; goods by drugs
items.take: BEA's advance estimate shows Q3 consumer spending rose in both services and goods, with real GDP up at a 3.4% annual rate. Within services the increase was led by health care (mainly hospitals and outpatient services) and food services and accommodations (mainly purchased meals and beverages). Within goods it was led by other nondurable goods, mainly prescription drugs. AlphaGen read: the spending gains BEA highlights are concentrated in medical care, dining out and drugs.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)

items.headline: BEA: Q3 export decline led by petroleum; imports led by capital goods
items.take: BEA's advance Q3 GDP estimate lists a decrease in exports among the offsets to growth, and says it primarily reflected a decrease in goods led by petroleum and related products. Imports, a subtraction in GDP, increased, with capital goods except automotive the largest contributor. Real GDP rose at a 3.4% annual rate in Q3, versus 2.2% in Q2. AlphaGen read: the trade drag in the quarter came from lower energy exports and higher equipment imports.
items.source_name: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)

items.take: FRED shows the 30-year constant-maturity Treasury yield at 5.40% on Nov. 19, versus 5.43% on Nov. 12 and 5.47% on Nov. 13. That is 0.07 point below the Nov. 13 reading in the latest observations. AlphaGen read: long-end yields eased through the week but stayed above 5.4%.
