items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Fed: UCLA wins 23rd College Fed Challenge; Chicago second, Maryland third
items.take: The Federal Reserve said the University of California, Los Angeles won the 23rd annual national College Fed Challenge on Nov. 20, with the University of Chicago in second place and the University of Maryland, College Park in third. The competition drew 141 schools from 34 states, the most in its history, and Chairman Kevin Warsh said the students "took on the same big questions we policymakers face." AlphaGen read: the contest is educational and carries no policy signal.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board

items.take: FRED shows the 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.15% on Nov. 20, versus 2.24% on Nov. 13 and 2.16% on Nov. 19. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.04% on Nov. 19 and the 10-year TIPS real yield was 2.88%, a 2.16-point gap that matches that day's 2.16% breakeven. AlphaGen read: the market-implied inflation compensation for the next decade has eased over the past week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

items.headline: Energy Transfer completes $2.7B senior notes offering across three maturities
items.take: Energy Transfer LP said it completed its underwritten public offering on Nov. 20 of $900M each of 5.450% notes due 2032, 5.900% notes due 2037 and 6.550% notes due 2057, or $2.7B in total. The notes were issued under a Thirteenth Supplemental Indenture dated Nov. 20, 2026. items.source_name: Energy Transfer LP, Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Baker Hughes files Chart Industries Q2 financials: sales $985.6M vs $1,082.3M
items.take: Baker Hughes filed an 8-K with unaudited Chart Industries statements showing Q2 2026 sales of $985.6M versus $1,082.3M a year earlier, an 8.9% decline, and operating income of $92.4M versus $169.5M. AlphaGen read: the figures are pre-closing Chart results under Chart's own accounting policies.
items.source_name: Baker Hughes Co, Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: LyondellBasell board approves retention awards for two executives
items.take: LyondellBasell said its board approved one-time retention awards on Nov. 18: a $2,000,000 cash award for Kimberly Foley, payable if she remains employed through Dec. 31, 2027, and restricted stock units with a $750,000 target value for CFO Agustin Izquierdo, cliff-vesting on the third anniversary of grant. The company described the awards as meant to promote leadership continuity during its ongoing portfolio transformation.
items.source_name: LyondellBasell Industries N.V., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: BoE market group minutes cite energy, AI debt financing, hedge-fund leverage
items.take: The Bank of England published minutes of its Nov. 18 Market Participants Group meeting on Nov. 19. Participants noted the resilience of UK growth despite the energy shock, which was broadly seen to have strengthened the case for higher rates, with the November increase widely expected, and discussed vulnerabilities including elevated hedge-fund leverage, sovereign debt pressures and cyber risks. AlphaGen read: the minutes tie energy prices, AI-related investment and leverage together as themes under discussion.
items.source_name: Bank of England, Market Participants Group minutes

items.headline: UK regulators propose cyber resilience guidance as October incident reports rise
items.take: The Bank of England, FCA and PRA proposed new guidance on Nov. 19 to help financial firms prepare for and recover from cyber incidents. The release says October 2026 saw the second-highest monthly number of cyber incidents reported to the FCA in five years, 52% above the previous 18-month peak recorded in May 2025. items.headline: Cook: generative AI used by 25% to 45% of working-age adults in rich economies
items.take: In a Nov. 20 speech in Santiago, Governor Lisa Cook said recent work finds generative AI use among the working-age population ranges from roughly 25% to 45% across higher-income economies, including Chile, a pace that exceeds personal-computer adoption at a comparable stage. She cited IMF analysis suggesting advanced economies may capture a disproportionate share of AI-driven productivity growth over the next decade. She noted Chile is the world's largest copper producer and second-largest lithium producer, minerals increasingly central to AI-related power transmission and energy storage. AlphaGen read: Cook tied commodity-linked economies to the pace of the AI buildout.

items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 5.07% and the Secured Overnight Financing Rate at 3.90% on Nov. 18. The difference is 1.17 percentage points. AlphaGen read: the gap measures how much the market pays for ten years of duration over overnight funding.

items.take: ICE BofA indexes in FRED show the U.S. high-yield option-adjusted spread at 3.47 percentage points and the investment-grade spread at 0.93 on Nov. 18. The gap between them was 2.54 points, versus 2.51 on Nov. 17. AlphaGen read: both spreads moved wider on the day, with high yield moving more.

items.take: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.28% in the week of Nov. 19, up from 7.11% on Nov. 12, in FRED data. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.07% on Nov. 18, which puts the gap at 2.21 percentage points. AlphaGen read: dates differ by a day, so treat the gap as approximate.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Lagarde: digital euro aimed at 2029 issuance if law passes by end-2026
items.take: In a Nov. 20 speech in Frankfurt, ECB President Christine Lagarde said international card schemes handle more than 60% of euro area card payments and 14 of the 21 euro area countries have no domestic scheme. She said that if legislation is adopted by the end of this year, the ECB aims to be ready for a first digital euro issuance in 2029. For Europe, the payments push is a sovereignty argument as much as a technology one.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Lagarde: tokenised assets ~€23B in March; ESM settled €1B bond on Pontes
items.take: Lagarde said the market for tokenised assets was worth around €23 billion worldwide in March, five times its size a year earlier. The ECB launched Pontes in September to settle tokenised transactions in central bank money, and the European Stability Mechanism settled a €1 billion digitally native bond on it earlier this month. The ECB is positioning settlement infrastructure as the common standard before platforms diverge.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Lagarde: EUREP repo facility made permanent in February; 30+ central banks interested
items.take: Lagarde said the ECB made EUREP, its repo facility for central banks, permanent in February and open to central banks worldwide, and that more than 30 central banks have already expressed interest. She also cited the linking of TIPS with fast payment systems in other regions and work to keep swap lines fit for purpose. The measures are aimed at making the euro easier to use abroad.
items.source_name: European Central Bank

items.headline: Merck: Glocer to retire from board in May 2027; Baker named lead director
items.take: Merck said Thomas H. Glocer intends to retire from its Board at the May 2027 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. The independent directors appointed Douglas M. Baker, Jr., a director since 2022, as independent lead director effective Jan. 1, 2027. The announcement was a governance change and did not include financial guidance.
items.source_name: Merck & Co. (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Air Products to nominate Carol Williams; two directors won't stand in 2027
items.take: Air Products said it will nominate Carol Williams, who spent 34 years at Dow, as an independent director candidate at its 2027 Annual Meeting. It also said Jessica Trocchi Graziano and Bhavesh (Bob) Patel will not stand for re-election and will retire when their terms conclude. The board refresh is the substance of the release; no financial figures were given.
items.source_name: Air Products and Chemicals (SEC Form 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: FRED: 10-year yield 0.73 point above 3-month bill on Nov. 18, from 0.78 on Nov. 16
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.07% and the 3-month yield at 4.34% on Nov. 18, a gap of 0.73 percentage point. On Nov. 16 the 10-year was 5.12% and the 3-month 4.34%, a 0.78-point gap; on Nov. 13 it was 5.15% against 4.32%, or 0.83. The gap narrowed because the 10-year fell while the bill yield held, a bond-market move that left short-term rates anchored.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: FRED: 2-year yield 0.46 point above 3-month bill on Nov. 18; 2-year 4.80%
items.take: FRED reports the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.80% and the 3-month at 4.34% on Nov. 18, so the 2-year sits 0.46 percentage point higher (AlphaGen calculation). The 2-year was 4.88% on Nov. 13 against a 4.32% bill, a 0.56-point gap. A narrower gap means the market is pricing a less steep path for short-term rates than it was a few days ago.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Core CPI index 339.900 in October, up 0.30%; 3-month pace 3.7% annualized
items.take: FRED's seasonally adjusted CPI excluding food and energy (1982-84=100) was 339.900 in October, up 0.30% from 338.896 in September; September's gain was 0.33%. Since July's 336.789 the index has risen 0.92%, or 3.7% at an annual rate (AlphaGen calculation). Core prices are still rising at a pace above the Fed's 2% goal.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Industrial production index 103.395 in October, down 0.43% on the month, up 2.1% on the year
items.take: FRED's total industrial production index (2017=100) was 103.3954 in October, down 0.43% from 103.8458 in September, after a 0.73% rise in September. Against October 2025's 101.2195 it is up 2.1% (AlphaGen calculations). Factory, mining and utility output slipped in October but remains above its year-earlier level.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Germany's 10-year yield 3.42% in October, down from 3.47%; UK 1.92 points higher
items.take: FRED's OECD-sourced long-term government bond series shows Germany at 3.42% in October, down from 3.47% in September and up from 2.62% a year earlier. The UK reading was 5.34%, which puts it 1.92 percentage points above Germany, versus 1.77 in September (AlphaGen calculations). British borrowing costs have risen faster than German ones over the past month.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Bath & Body Works Q3 net sales $1,577M, down 1.0%; diluted EPS $0.19 vs $0.37
items.take: Bath & Body Works reported third-quarter net sales of $1,577 million versus $1,594 million, a decrease of 1.0%, with operating income of $108 million versus $161 million. Diluted EPS was $0.19 versus $0.37; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.26 versus $0.35. Lower operating income on slightly lower sales shows costs outpacing revenue in the quarter.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Bath & Body Works: stores down 4.3%, direct up 2.6%, international up 39.3% in Q3
items.take: Q3 sales in U.S. and Canada stores were $1,169 million versus $1,222 million (-4.3%), direct U.S. and Canada sales were $307 million versus $299 million (+2.6%), and International and Other was $101 million versus $73 million (+39.3%). Stores still made up about 74% of Q3 net sales ($1,169M of $1,577M), so store traffic remains the main swing factor.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Bath & Body Works raises FY26 sales outlook; sees net sales down 3.4% to 2.1%
items.take: The company now expects fiscal 2026 net sales to decline between 3.4% and 2.1% versus $7,291 million in fiscal 2025, and Q4 net sales to decline between 5.5% and 2.0% versus $2,724 million, with Q4 diluted EPS of $1.41 to $1.61. It also announced a new $500 million share repurchase program that may begin after the existing January 2025 program is completed. Even the raised full-year range still implies lower sales than last year.
items.source_name: Bath & Body Works (GlobeNewswire release)

items.headline: Fed publishes revised 2027 FOMC schedule: eight meetings, Oct. 26-27 set for strategy
items.take: The Federal Reserve's revised tentative 2027 schedule, released Nov. 12, lists meetings on Jan. 26-27, Mar. 16-17, Apr. 27-28, Jun. 8-9, Jul. 27-28, Sep. 14-15, Oct. 26-27 and Nov. 16-17, with the first 2028 meeting on Jan. 25-26. The Committee will announce its decision on the second day of each meeting except Oct. 26-27, which is dedicated to broad monetary policy strategy issues. The calendar fixes the dates markets will watch for 2027 rate decisions.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board

items.headline: CPI all-items index up 1.4% in three months to October, a 5.7% annual pace
items.take: FRED's seasonally adjusted CPI index was 337.476 in October, up 0.35% from 336.298 in September and 1.40% from 332.813 in July. Compounded over four quarters, the July–October gain equals a 5.7% annual rate. AlphaGen read: the headline index has run well ahead of the core index, which rose 0.92% over the same three months, a 3.7% annual pace.
items.source_name: BLS Consumer Price Index via FRED (CPIAUCSL, CPILFESL)

items.headline: Core PCE index 130.902 in September, up 0.32% on the month
items.take: FRED's core PCE price index (excluding food and energy) was 130.902 in September, up from 130.489 in August and 129.969 in June. That is a 0.32% monthly gain and a 2.9% annualized pace over June–September. AlphaGen read: core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, has been running below the 3.7% annualized pace of core CPI over July–October, though the two cover different months and baskets.
items.source_name: BEA Personal Consumption Expenditures via FRED (PCEPILFE)

items.headline: Unemployment rate 4.1% in October, 7.1M unemployed; range 4.1%–4.3% since March
items.take: BLS said the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1% in October and the number of unemployed people, at 7.1 million, was little changed. The rate has stayed in a narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March, and FRED shows 4.2% in September and 4.1% in July and August. AlphaGen read: a labor market that is not loosening keeps the Fed's focus on inflation.
items.source_name: BLS Employment Situation, October 2026

items.headline: BBB corporate spread 1.16 points on Nov. 18, up from 1.11 on Nov. 13

The broad investment-grade index spread was 0.93 on Nov. 18, so BBB paper carried 0.23 point more than the index. AlphaGen read: the BBB gap widened 5 basis points in three sessions.
items.source_name: ICE Data Indices via FRED (BAMLC0A4CBBB, BAMLC0A0CM)

items.headline: Census revises Quarterly Services estimates with the Q3 advance release
items.take: Census says that effective with the November 2026 advance release for the third quarter of 2026, not seasonally adjusted Quarterly Services estimates were revised for historical corrections and the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey results. The seasonally adjusted Selected Services Total was also revised, with new seasonal factors. AlphaGen read: BEA uses the survey in its GDP estimates, so the revisions bear on the Nov. 25 GDP second estimate.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, Quarterly Services Survey

items.headline: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B in cash
items.take: In an 8-K, Intuit said it entered an Equity and Asset Purchase Agreement on Nov. 19 to sell its Mailchimp business to Bending Spoons US Inc. for an all-cash base purchase price of $3.68 billion, subject to customary adjustments. Intuit also agreed to invest about $368 million of the purchase price in Bending Spoons S.p.A. for 8,818,595 newly issued ordinary shares, and closing is expected in early calendar 2027. AlphaGen read: the reinvestment equals 10% of the base price, so Intuit's net cash from the sale would be lower than the headline figure.
items.source_name: Intuit Inc., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

It had been 7.18% on Nov. 5 and 7.24% on Oct. 29. AlphaGen read: the weekly reading reverses the declines of the prior three weeks and returns to roughly the late-October level.

items.headline: Duke Energy sells $875M of 6.05% senior notes due 2036
items.take: Duke Energy filed an underwriting agreement dated Nov. 17, 2026 for $875,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 6.05% Senior Notes due 2036, with MUFG, PNC, Santander, SMBC Nikko, U.S. Bancorp and Wells Fargo as representatives of the underwriters. items.source_name: Duke Energy Corporation, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Edwards Lifesciences signs new $750M five-year revolving credit facility
items.take: Edwards Lifesciences said on Nov. 19 it entered an Amended and Restated Five Year Credit Agreement providing a $750 million multi-currency unsecured revolving facility maturing Nov. 19, 2031, with an option to add up to $375 million more. Borrowings bear interest at SOFR or a base rate plus a margin based on leverage ratio or debt ratings. AlphaGen read: the company describes the move as a planned refreshment of its bank facility, replacing the July 2022 agreement.
items.source_name: Edwards Lifesciences Corp., Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)
